sentences.zh: 自古后族，能以德禮進退、全宗保名者，鮮矣。

translations.literal: From antiquity among affinal kin of empresses, those who could advance and withdraw by virtue and ritual propriety, preserving their clan and safeguarding their reputation—such have been few.
translations.idiomatic: Since ancient times, few families of empresses have managed to rise and fall with propriety, keep their house intact, and preserve a good name.

sentences.zh: 蓋恃宮掖之寵，接宴私之歡，高爵厚祿驕其內，聲色服玩惑於外；

translations.literal: This was because they relied on favor in the inner palace, joined in private banquet pleasures, were made arrogant within by high titles and generous salaries, and were beguiled without by music, beauty, dress, and curios;
translations.idiomatic: They leaned on palace favor and private revelry; within, lofty rank and rich stipends bred arrogance, while without, music, women, finery, and luxuries led them astray.

sentences.zh: 莫知師友之訓，不達危亡之道。

translations.literal: They knew not the instruction of teachers and friends, and did not comprehend the path to peril and ruin.
translations.idiomatic: They never learned the lessons of mentors and companions, nor understood how dynasties fall.

sentences.zh: 故以中才處之，罕不覆敗；

translations.literal: Thus when placed in office with merely average talent, rarely did they escape overthrow;
translations.idiomatic: Given only middling ability, they seldom escaped ruin.

sentences.zh: 亦由重植之木，自然顛披也。

translations.literal: It is also like a heavily planted tree that naturally topples.
translations.idiomatic: It is like a tree grown too tall—it must eventually fall.

sentences.zh: 明哲之君，知驕侈之易滿，榮寵之難保；

translations.literal: Wise and perspicacious rulers know that arrogance and extravagance are easily sated, and glory and favor are hard to preserve;
translations.idiomatic: A clear-sighted sovereign knows that pride and excess are soon exhausted, while honor and favor are hard to hold.

sentences.zh: 授任各當其才，祿位不過其量；

translations.literal: They appoint each to duties matching his talent, and grant stipends and rank not beyond his measure;
translations.idiomatic: They assign offices suited to each man's ability and never grant salary or rank beyond what he deserves.

sentences.zh: 告之以天命不易，誡之以大義滅親；

translations.literal: They tell them that the Mandate of Heaven is not to be taken lightly, and warn them with the great principle of putting the state before kinship;
translations.idiomatic: They teach that Heaven's mandate is not to be trifled with and admonish them with the duty to subordinate kin to the greater good.

sentences.zh: 使居無過之地，永享不貲之福，與國終始，不失其所以親也。

translations.literal: They cause them to dwell where they commit no fault, forever enjoy uncountable blessings, and with the state from beginning to end do not lose the basis of their closeness to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Thus they keep their kin blameless, blessed for life, bound to the realm from first to last without forfeiting the ties that make them family.

sentences.zh: 《易》曰：「震來虩虩，恐致福也。」

translations.literal: The Book of Changes says: "Thunder comes, fear and trembling; through fear blessings are attained."
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Changes says: "Thunder comes with dread—through fear one may win blessing."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「婦子嘻嘻，失家節也。」

translations.literal: It also says: "Wife and children titter and laugh—the family loses its proper order."
translations.idiomatic: It also says: "When wife and children only laugh and play, the household loses its discipline."

sentences.zh: 與其愛而失節，曷若懼而致福？

translations.literal: Rather than loving them and losing order, how much better to fear and thereby attain blessing?
translations.idiomatic: Better to inspire fear and gain blessing than to indulge with love and lose all restraint.

sentences.zh: 魏氏懲漢人之敗，著矯枉之法：幼主嗣位，母后不得臨朝；

translations.literal: Wei punished the failure of the Han and set forth laws to correct excess: when a young lord succeeded, the empress dowager might not hold court;
translations.idiomatic: Learning from the Han collapse, Wei enacted corrective statutes: when a child emperor succeeded, the empress dowager could not govern from court;

sentences.zh: 外氏無功，時主不得封爵。

translations.literal: kin on the mother's side without merit—the reigning lord might not ennoble them.
translations.idiomatic: and maternal kin without merit could not be ennobled by the reigning sovereign.

sentences.zh: 雖曰刻薄，而卞、甄之族，竟無大過。

translations.literal: Though called harsh, yet the Bian and Zhen clans in the end committed no great fault.
translations.idiomatic: Harsh as these rules seemed, the Bian and Zhen clans never committed any grave offense.

sentences.zh: 皇唐受命，長孫、竇氏以勛賢任職，而武氏、韋氏以盈滿致覆。

translations.literal: When the Tang received the mandate, the Zhangsun and Dou clans took office for meritorious virtue, while the Wu and Wei clans through fullness were overthrown.
translations.idiomatic: When Tang received Heaven's mandate, the Zhangsun and Dou served for merit and talent, while the Wu and Wei were destroyed because they had grown too full of power.

sentences.zh: 夫廢興者，豈天命哉，蓋人事也！

translations.literal: Rise and fall—how could it be the Mandate of Heaven? It is human affairs!
translations.idiomatic: Whether a house rises or falls—is that fate? It is what men make of it!

sentences.zh: 竇威、長孫無忌各自有傳，其餘載其得失，為《外戚傳》，以存鑒誡焉。

translations.literal: Dou Wei and Zhangsun Wuji each have their own biographies; the rest record their gains and losses in the "Biographies of Affinal Kin," to preserve warning and admonition.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Wei and Zhangsun Wuji have separate biographies; the rest are gathered here in the Affinal Kin, that their successes and failures may serve as warning.

sentences.zh: 獨孤懷恩

translations.literal: = Dugu Huai'en =
translations.idiomatic: Dugu Huai'en

sentences.zh: 獨孤懷恩，元貞皇后弟之子也。

translations.literal: Dugu Huai'en was the son of the younger brother of Empress Yuanzhen.
translations.idiomatic: Dugu Huai'en was a nephew of Empress Yuanzhen.

sentences.zh: 父整，隋涿郡太守。

translations.literal: His father Zheng was Administrator of Zhuo Prefecture under the Sui.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zheng had been prefect of Zhuo commandery under the Sui.

sentences.zh: 懷恩幼時，以獻皇后之侄，養於宮中。

translations.literal: In his youth Huai'en, as nephew of Empress Xian, was reared in the palace.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy, being a nephew of Empress Xian, Huai'en was raised inside the palace.

sentences.zh: 後仕為鄠縣令。

translations.literal: Later he served as magistrate of E County.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as magistrate of E county.

sentences.zh: 高祖平京城，授長安令。

translations.literal: When Gaozu pacified the capital, he was appointed magistrate of Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu took the capital, Huai'en was made magistrate of Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 在職嚴明，甚得時譽。

translations.literal: In office he was strict and clear-minded, and won great contemporary praise.
translations.idiomatic: In office he was strict and fair, and won wide praise.

sentences.zh: 及高祖受禪，擢拜工部尚書。

translations.literal: When Gaozu received the abdication, he was promoted and appointed Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu took the throne, Huai'en was promoted to Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 時虞州刺史韋義節擊堯君素於蒲州，而義節文吏怯懦，頻戰不利。

translations.literal: At that time the prefect of Yu, Wei Yijie, was attacking Yao Junsu at Pu Prefecture, but Yijie, a civil clerk, was timid and cowardly, and repeatedly fought without success.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Wei Yijie, prefect of Yu, was besieging Yao Junsu at Pu, but Yijie was a timid civil official and kept losing in battle.

sentences.zh: 高祖遣懷恩代總其眾。

translations.literal: Gaozu sent Huai'en to replace him and take overall command of the troops.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu sent Huai'en to replace him and take command of the army.

sentences.zh: 懷恩督兵城下，為賊所拒，頻戰不利。

translations.literal: Huai'en directed troops beneath the walls and was repelled by the rebels; repeatedly he fought without success.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'en led troops to the walls but was beaten back; battle after battle went against him.

sentences.zh: 高祖切讓之，因是怨望。

translations.literal: Gaozu sharply reproached him, and because of this he harbored resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu rebuked him harshly, and from that time Huai'en nursed a grievance.

sentences.zh: 高祖嘗戲之曰：「弟姑子悉為天子，次當舅子乎？」

translations.literal: Gaozu once jested with him, saying: "Your sister's sons have all become Son of Heaven—should the next be your sister's son?"
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu once teased him: "Your sister's sons have all become emperors—should the next be your sister's son?"

sentences.zh: 懷恩遂自以為符命，每扼腕曰：「我家豈女獨富貴耶？」

translations.literal: Huai'en then took this as a sign of destiny; clenching his wrist he would say: "Must our house alone be enriched through women?"
translations.idiomatic: Huai'en took this as a portent of destiny and would clench his fist, saying, "Must our house prosper only through women?"

sentences.zh: 由是陰圖異計。

translations.literal: From this he secretly plotted a divergent design.
translations.idiomatic: From then on he secretly plotted treason.

sentences.zh: 時虞鄉南山多群盜。

translations.literal: At that time on the southern mountains of Yu district there were many bandit gangs.
translations.idiomatic: At that time bandit bands were numerous in the southern hills of Yu district.

sentences.zh: 劉武周將宋金剛寇陷澮州，高祖悉發關中卒以隸太宗，屯於柏壁。

translations.literal: Liu Wuzhou's general Song Jingang raided and captured Fen Prefecture; Gaozu sent out all the troops of Guanzhong to serve under Taizong, encamped at Baiyu.
translations.idiomatic: Song Jingang, a general of Liu Wuzhou, seized Fen; Gaozu sent every soldier in Guanzhong to serve under the Prince of Qin and encamped at Baiyu.

sentences.zh: 懷恩遂與解縣令榮靜、前五原縣主簿元君寶謀引王行本兵及武周連和，與山賊劫永豐倉而斷柏壁糧道，割河東地以啗武周。

translations.literal: Huai'en then with the magistrate of Jie, Rong Jing, and the former registrar of Wuyuan, Yuan Junbao, plotted to bring in Wang Xingben's troops and join with Wuzhou, together with the mountain bandits to raid Yongfeng granary and cut the grain route to Baiyu, ceding Hedong territory to feed Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'en conspired with Rong Jing, magistrate of Jie, and Yuan Junbao, former registrar of Wuyuan, to bring in Wang Xingben's army, ally with Wuzhou, join the hill bandits in raiding Yongfeng granary, sever Baiyu's supply line, and cede Hedong to Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 事臨發，會夏縣人呂崇茂殺縣令，據縣起兵，應武周。

translations.literal: As the affair was on the verge of execution, it happened that Lü Chongmao of Xia County killed the magistrate, seized the county and raised troops, responding to Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Just as the plot was about to unfold, Lü Chongmao of Xia county killed the magistrate, seized the county, and rose in support of Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 高祖遣懷恩與永安王孝基、陜州總管於筠、內史侍郎唐儉攻崇茂。

translations.literal: Gaozu sent Huai'en with Prince Yong'an Xiaoji, the commander of Shan Prefecture Yu Yun, and the Vice Director of the Secretariat Tang Jian to attack Chongmao.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu sent Huai'en with Prince Yong'an Xiaoji, Yu Yun, military governor of Shan, and Tang Jian, vice director of the Secretariat, to attack Chongmao.

sentences.zh: 宋金剛潛兵來襲，諸將盡沒。

translations.literal: Song Jingang secretly brought troops to strike; the generals were all destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Song Jingang struck in secret and wiped out the entire force.

sentences.zh: 君寶與開府劉讓亦同陷於賊中，遂泄懷恩之謀。

translations.literal: Junbao and the Defender-in-Chief Liu Rang also fell together into the rebels' hands, and thus revealed Huai'en's plot.
translations.idiomatic: Junbao and Liu Rang, a defender-in-chief, were also captured, and they disclosed Huai'en's conspiracy.

sentences.zh: 既而懷恩逃歸，高祖復令率師攻蒲州。

translations.literal: Thereafter Huai'en fled back; Gaozu again ordered him to lead troops to attack Pu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'en escaped and returned; Gaozu again ordered him to lead an army against Pu.

sentences.zh: 唐儉在賊中，說賊將尉遲敬德，請使讓還，連和罷兵，遂使發其事。

translations.literal: Tang Jian was among the rebels; he persuaded the rebel general Yuchi Jingde to request that Rang be returned, to join in alliance and cease hostilities, and thus caused the affair to be exposed.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Jian, still a prisoner, persuaded the rebel general Yuchi Jingde to send Liu Rang back in exchange for peace—and so the plot came to light.

sentences.zh: 會堯君素為其下所殺，小帥王行本以蒲州降，懷恩勒兵入據其城。

translations.literal: It happened that Yao Junsu was killed by his subordinates; the minor commander Wang Xingben surrendered Pu Prefecture, and Huai'en led troops in and occupied the city.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Junsu was killed by his own men; the minor commander Wang Xingben surrendered Pu, and Huai'en marched in and took the city.

sentences.zh: 高祖將濟河，已御舟矣，會讓至，乃使召懷恩，懷恩不知事已泄，輕舟來赴。

translations.literal: Gaozu was about to cross the river and had already boarded the boat when Rang arrived; he then sent to summon Huai'en. Huai'en did not know the affair had been exposed and came in a light boat.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu was about to cross the river and had already boarded his boat when Rang arrived; he sent for Huai'en, who, not knowing the plot was known, came swiftly in a small craft.

sentences.zh: 及中流而執之，收其黨按驗，遂誅之，時年三十六，籍沒基家。

translations.literal: Midstream he was seized; his partisans were arrested and examined, and he was then executed. He was thirty-six years old; his household property was confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: Midstream they seized him, arrested his accomplices, and put him to death. He was thirty-six; his family's property was confiscated.

sentences.zh: 竇德明

translations.literal: = Dou Deming =
translations.idiomatic: Dou Deming

sentences.zh: 竇德明，太穆順聖皇后兄之孫也。

translations.literal: Dou Deming was a grandson of the elder brother of Empress Taimu Shunsheng.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Deming was a grandson of Empress Taimu's elder brother.

sentences.zh: 祖照，尚後魏文帝女義陽公主，封鉅鹿公。

translations.literal: His grandfather Zhao married Princess Yiyang, daughter of Emperor Wen of Later Wei, and was enfeoffed as Duke of Julu.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Zhao married Princess Yiyang, daughter of Emperor Wen of Northern Wei, and was enfeoffed as Duke of Julu.

sentences.zh: 父彥，襲父封，仕隋為西平郡守。

translations.literal: His father Yan inherited his father's enfeoffment and served the Sui as Administrator of Xiping commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yan inherited the title and served the Sui as prefect of Xiping commandery.

sentences.zh: 德明少師事陳留王孝逸，頗涉文史。

translations.literal: Deming in youth studied under Wang Xiaoyi, Prince of Chenliu, and was well versed in letters and history.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Deming studied under Wang Xiaoyi, Prince of Chenliu, and gained a solid grounding in literature and history.

sentences.zh: 會漢王諒作亂，遣其將綦良攻黎州。

translations.literal: It happened that Prince Han Liang rebelled and sent his general Qi Liang to attack Li Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Han Liang rebelled, he sent his general Qi Liang to attack Li prefecture.

sentences.zh: 德明時年十八，募得五千人，倍道而進，號令嚴整，一戰破之。

translations.literal: Deming was then eighteen; he recruited five thousand men, advanced by double marches, kept orders strict and orderly, and in one battle routed them.
translations.idiomatic: Deming was eighteen; he raised five thousand men, forced the march, kept discipline tight, and routed the enemy in a single battle.

sentences.zh: 以功累拜齊王府屬，坐事免。

translations.literal: For merit he was repeatedly promoted to an attendant of the Prince of Qi's household, but through an offense was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: For this feat he rose to an appointment on the staff of the Prince of Qi, but later was dismissed after an offense.

sentences.zh: 及義師圍長安，永安王孝基、襄邑王神符、江夏王道宗及高祖之婿竇誕、趙慈景並繫獄，隋將衛文升、陰世師欲殺之。

translations.literal: When the righteous army besieged Chang'an, Prince Yong'an Xiaoji, Prince of Xiangyi Shenfu, Prince of Jiangxia Daozong, and Gaozu's sons-in-law Dou Dan and Zhao Cijing were all imprisoned; the Sui generals Wei Wensheng and Yin Shishi wished to kill them.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebel army besieged Chang'an, Princes Yong'an Xiaoji, Xiangyi Shenfu, and Jiangxia Daozong, together with Gaozu's sons-in-law Dou Dan and Zhao Cijing, were all in prison; the Sui generals Wei Wensheng and Yin Shishi meant to execute them.

sentences.zh: 德明謂文升曰：「罪不在此輩，殺之無傷於彼，適足招怨。」

translations.literal: Deming said to Wensheng: "The crime is not with these men; killing them would not harm the other side but would only invite resentment."
translations.idiomatic: Deming told Wensheng, "These men are not guilty; killing them would not hurt the enemy but would only breed hatred."

sentences.zh: 文升乃止。

translations.literal: Wensheng then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Wensheng held his hand.

sentences.zh: 及謁見高祖，竟不自言，時人稱其長者。

translations.literal: When he had an audience with Gaozu, he never spoke of it himself; people of the time praised him as a man of mature character.
translations.idiomatic: When he later met Gaozu, he never mentioned what he had done; contemporaries called him a man of true dignity.

sentences.zh: 武德初，拜考功郎中。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wude he was appointed Director in the Bureau of Appointments.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Wude era he was made a director in the Bureau of Appointments.

sentences.zh: 從太宗擊王世充，頻有戰功，封顯武男。

translations.literal: He followed Taizong in attacking Wang Shichong, repeatedly had battle merit, and was enfeoffed as Baron of Xianwu.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Taizong against Wang Shichong, won repeated victories, and was enfeoffed as Baron of Xianwu.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，歷常、愛二州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenguan he successively served as prefect of Chang and Ai.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhenguan he served in turn as prefect of Chang and Ai prefectures.

sentences.zh: 尋卒。

translations.literal: Soon after he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon after.

sentences.zh: 弟德玄，高宗時為左相。

translations.literal: His younger brother Dexuan, in the time of Gaozong, was Left Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Dexuan served as left chancellor under Gaozong.

sentences.zh: 德玄子懷貞。

translations.literal: Dexuan's son was Huaizhen.
translations.idiomatic: Dexuan's son was Huaizhen.

sentences.zh: 懷貞，少有名譽，時兄弟宗族，並以輿馬為事，懷貞獨折節自修，衣服儉素。

translations.literal: Huaizhen in youth had a fine reputation; at the time brothers and clansmen all made carriages and horses their business, but Huaizhen alone restrained himself in self-cultivation and wore plain, simple clothing.
translations.idiomatic: Huaizhen was known from youth for integrity; while kinsmen flaunted carriages and horses, he alone lived modestly in plain dress.

sentences.zh: 聖歷中為清河令，治有能名。

translations.literal: During Shenglu he was magistrate of Qinghe; his governance had a reputation for ability.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shenglu era he was magistrate of Qinghe and earned a name for capable rule.

sentences.zh: 俄歷越州都督、揚州大都督府長史，所在皆以清幹著稱，

translations.literal: Soon he successively served as military governor of Yue and chief administrator of the Grand Protectorate of Yang; wherever he went he was known for purity and efficiency.
translations.idiomatic: He soon served as governor of Yue and chief administrator of Yang prefecture, winning praise everywhere for probity and competence.

sentences.zh: 累遷御史大夫，兼檢校雍州長史。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Censor-in-Chief and concurrently Acting Chief Administrator of Yong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to censor-in-chief and concurrently acting chief administrator of Yong prefecture.

sentences.zh: 時韋庶人及安樂公主等干預朝政。

translations.literal: At that time the Deposed Consort Wei and Princess Anle and others interfered in court affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Empress Wei (while still consort) and Princess Anle meddled in government.

sentences.zh: 懷貞每諂順委曲取容，改名從一，以避后父之諱，自是名稱日損。

translations.literal: Huaizhen always flattered and bent himself to win favor; he changed his name to Congyi to avoid the taboo on the empress's father's name, and from this his reputation daily declined.
translations.idiomatic: Huaizhen flattered and curried favor at every turn; he changed his name to Congyi to avoid the empress's father's taboo name, and his reputation sank further.

sentences.zh: 庶人微時乳母王氏，本蠻婢也，特封莒國夫人，嫁為懷貞妻。

translations.literal: The Deposed Consort's wet nurse in her humble days, Lady Wang, was originally a barbarian slave; she was specially enfeoffed as Lady of Ju state and married to become Huaizhen's wife.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Wang, the empress's former wet nurse, had been a barbarian slave; she was ennobled as Lady of Ju and married to Huaizhen.

sentences.zh: 俗謂乳母之婿為阿沄，懷貞每因謁見之次及進表疏，列在官位，必曰「皇后阿沄」，時人或以「國沄」呼之，初無慚色。

translations.literal: Common speech calls a wet nurse's son-in-law "Ayun"; whenever Huaizhen on occasions of audience or in submitting memorials listed his official position, he invariably said "the Empress's Ayun," and people of the time sometimes called him "State Ayun"; at first he showed no shame.
translations.idiomatic: A wet nurse's son-in-law was vulgarly called "Ayun"; in audiences and memorials Huaizhen always signed himself "the Empress's Ayun," and people mocked him as "State Ayun"—yet he felt no shame.

sentences.zh: 宦官用權，懷貞尤所畏敬，每視事聽訟，見無須者，誤以接之。

translations.literal: Eunuchs wielded power, and Huaizhen especially feared and honored them; whenever he held office and heard lawsuits, if he saw a beardless man he would mistakenly receive him with ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuchs held power, and Huaizhen feared them above all; when hearing cases, he would bow to any beardless man, mistaking him for a eunuch.

sentences.zh: 監察御史魏傳弓嘗以內常侍輔信義尤縱暴，將奏劾之。

translations.literal: The investigating censor Wei Chuanggong once, because the inner attendant Fu Xinyi was especially wanton and violent, was about to memorialize impeachment against him.
translations.idiomatic: Investigating censor Wei Chuanggong once prepared to impeach the inner attendant Fu Xinyi for his outrageous conduct.

sentences.zh: 懷貞曰：「輔常侍深為安樂公主所信任，權勢甚高，言成禍福，何得輒有彈糾？」

translations.literal: Huaizhen said: "Attendant Fu is deeply trusted by Princess Anle; his power is very high—his words make fortune or disaster. How can you rashly impeach him?"
translations.idiomatic: Huaizhen said, "Attendant Fu enjoys Princess Anle's deepest trust; his word makes or breaks men—how dare you impeach him?"

sentences.zh: 傳弓曰：「今王綱漸壞，君子道消，正由此輩擅權耳！

translations.literal: Chuanggong said: "Now the royal net is gradually ruined, the way of the gentleman fades—precisely because such men monopolize power!
translations.idiomatic: Chuanggong replied, "The royal order is crumbling and upright men are silenced—because of men like him!

sentences.zh: 若得今日殺之，明日受誅，無所恨。」

translations.literal: If I can kill him today and tomorrow receive execution, I have no regret."
translations.idiomatic: If I can kill him today and die tomorrow, I will not regret it."

sentences.zh: 懷貞無以答，但固止之。

translations.literal: Huaizhen had nothing to answer but firmly stopped him.
translations.idiomatic: Huaizhen could only argue and forcibly restrain him.

sentences.zh: 韋庶人敗，左遷濠州司馬。

translations.literal: When the Deposed Consort Wei was overthrown, he was demoted and transferred as military aide of Hao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Wei fell, Huaizhen was demoted to military aide of Hao prefecture.

sentences.zh: 尋擢授益州大都督府長史。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted and appointed chief administrator of the Grand Protectorate of Yi.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to chief administrator of Yi prefecture.

sentences.zh: 以附會太平公主，累拜侍中、兼御史大夫，代韋安石為尚書左僕射，監修國史，賜爵魏國公。

translations.literal: By attaching himself to Princess Taiping he was repeatedly promoted to Palace Attendant and concurrent Censor-in-Chief, replaced Wei Anshi as Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, supervised compilation of the national history, and was granted the title Duke of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Currying favor with Princess Taiping, he rose to palace attendant and censor-in-chief, replaced Wei Anshi as left vice director of the Secretariat, supervised the national history, and was made Duke of Wei.

sentences.zh: 睿宗為金仙、玉真二公主創立兩觀，料功甚多，時議皆以為不可。

translations.literal: Ruizong for the two princesses Jinxian and Yuzhen established two abbeys; the estimated labor was very great, and opinion at the time all held it inadvisable.
translations.idiomatic: Ruizong ordered two monasteries built for Princesses Jinxian and Yuzhen; the project was vast, and nearly everyone said it should not be done.

sentences.zh: 唯懷貞贊成其事，躬自監役。

translations.literal: Only Huaizhen approved the affair and personally supervised the labor.
translations.idiomatic: Only Huaizhen approved it and personally supervised construction.

sentences.zh: 懷貞族弟詹事司直維鍌謂懷貞曰：「兄位極臺袞，當思獻可替否，以輔明主。

translations.literal: Huaizhen's clansman, the Direct Clerk of the Household of the Heir Apparent Wei Chou, said to Huaizhen: "Elder brother, your position has reached the summit of the court; you ought to think of offering what is acceptable and replacing what is not, to assist the enlightened lord.
translations.idiomatic: His kinsman Wei Chou, a clerk in the heir apparent's household, said, "Brother, you stand at the pinnacle of power; you should counsel the throne, not flatter it.

sentences.zh: 奈何校量瓦木，廁跡工匠之間，欲令海內何所瞻仰也？」

translations.literal: Why measure tiles and timber and mingle your tracks among the craftsmen—what is there under Heaven for people to look up to?"
translations.idiomatic: Why measure tiles and timber and stand among laborers—what will the empire think of you?"

sentences.zh: 懷貞不能對，而監作如故。

translations.literal: Huaizhen could not reply, but supervised construction as before.
translations.idiomatic: Huaizhen had no answer but kept supervising as before.

sentences.zh: 時人為之語曰：「竇僕射前為韋氏國沄，後作公主邑丞。」

translations.literal: People of the time made a saying about him: "Vice Director Dou formerly was the Wei clan's State Ayun; afterward he became the princesses' district aide."
translations.idiomatic: People said of him: "Vice Director Dou was once the Wei clan's State Ayun; now he is the princesses' district clerk."

sentences.zh: 言懷貞伏事公主，同於邑官也，

translations.literal: This meant Huaizhen served the princesses like a district official.
translations.idiomatic: Meaning he served the princesses like a petty local official.

sentences.zh: 太平公主逆謀事泄，懷貞懼罪，投水而死。

translations.literal: When Princess Taiping's treasonous plot was exposed, Huaizhen feared punishment and threw himself into the water and died.
translations.idiomatic: When Princess Taiping's plot was exposed, Huaizhen, fearing punishment, drowned himself.

sentences.zh: 追戮其屍，改姓毒氏。

translations.literal: His corpse was pursued and punished; his surname was changed to the Poison clan.
translations.idiomatic: His corpse was posthumously punished and his clan name changed to Du (Poison).

sentences.zh: 德明族弟孝諶。

translations.literal: Deming's clansman Xiaochen.
translations.idiomatic: Deming's kinsman Xiaochen.

sentences.zh: 孝諶，刑部尚書誕之子，昭成順聖皇后父也。

translations.literal: Xiaochen was the son of Dan, Minister of Justice; he was the father of Empress Zhaocheng Shunsheng.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaochen was son of Dan, minister of justice, and father of Empress Zhaocheng.

sentences.zh: 則天時，歷太常少卿、潤州刺史，

translations.literal: In the time of Zetian he successively served as Vice Minister of Rites and prefect of Run.
translations.idiomatic: Under Empress Wu he served as vice minister of rites and prefect of Run.

sentences.zh: 后母龐氏被酷吏所陷，誣與后咒詛不道，孝諶左遷羅州司馬而卒。

translations.literal: The empress's mother, Lady Pang, was trapped by a cruel official who falsely charged her with the empress in cursing and impiety; Xiaochen was demoted and transferred as military aide of Luo Prefecture and died.
translations.idiomatic: The empress's mother Lady Pang was framed by a cruel official for witchcraft against the throne; Xiaochen was demoted to military aide of Luo and died there.

sentences.zh: 子希瑊、希球、希瓘，並流嶺南。

translations.literal: His sons Xizhen, Xiqiu, and Xichan were all exiled to Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Xizhen, Xiqiu, and Xichan were all exiled to the far south.

sentences.zh: 神龍初，隨例雪免。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shenlong, following precedent they were cleared and pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Shenlong restoration they were pardoned with the rest.

sentences.zh: 景雲年，追贈李諶太尉、邠國公，希瑊襲爵。

translations.literal: In the Jingyun era Li Chen was posthumously honored as Grand Marshal and Duke of Bin; Xizhen inherited the enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jingyun era Li Chen was posthumously made grand marshal and Duke of Bin; Xizhen inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 玄宗即位，加贈孝諶太保，希瑊等以舅氏，甚見優寵。

translations.literal: When Xuanzong took the throne, Xiaochen was further posthumously honored as Grand Guardian; Xizhen and the others, as maternal uncles, were greatly favored and indulged.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuanzong ascended the throne, Xiaochen was further honored as grand guardian; as the emperor's uncles, Xizhen and his brothers were lavishly favored.

sentences.zh: 希瑊累遷太子少傅、豳國公，尋卒。

translations.literal: Xizhen was repeatedly promoted to Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent and Duke of Bin state; soon after he died.
translations.idiomatic: Xizhen rose to junior tutor of the heir apparent and Duke of Bin; he died soon after.

sentences.zh: 希球官至太子賓客，封冀國公，卒。

translations.literal: Xiqiu reached the office of Guest of the Heir Apparent, was enfeoffed as Duke of Ji state, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Xiqiu became guest of the heir apparent and Duke of Ji; he died in office.

sentences.zh: 及卒，謚曰靖。

translations.literal: When he died, his posthumous title was Jing (Tranquil).
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously titled Tranquil (Jing).

sentences.zh: 希瓘初賜爵畢國公，後改名。

translations.literal: Xichan was initially enfeoffed as Duke of Bi state; later the title was changed.
translations.idiomatic: Xichan was first made Duke of Bi; the enfeoffment was later renamed.

sentences.zh: 初為左散騎常侍，及希球卒，因授開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: Initially he served as Left Regular Attendant of the Palace Horse; when Xiqiu died, he was accordingly appointed Commissioner with the Same Three Excellencies as an Opening Office.
translations.idiomatic: He first served as left attendant of the palace horse; when Xiqiu died, he was appointed commissioner with the same privileges as the three excellencies.

sentences.zh: 玄宗以早失太后，尤重外家，兄弟三人皆國公，食實封。

translations.literal: Because Xuanzong had lost his mother the empress dowager early, he especially valued his maternal kin; all three brothers were dukes with taxable fief households.
translations.idiomatic: Having lost his mother early, Xuanzong cherished his maternal relatives all the more; all three brothers became dukes with income-bearing fiefs.

sentences.zh: 子鍔，又尚玄宗女永昌長公主，恩寵賜賚，實為厚矣。

translations.literal: His son E also married Princess Yongchang, daughter of Xuanzong; favor and gifts were indeed lavish.
translations.idiomatic: His son E also married Xuanzong's daughter, Princess Yongchang; the favor and gifts showered on them were truly great.

sentences.zh: 而兄弟皆貪鄙，過自封植，又甚之，

translations.literal: Yet the brothers were all greedy and base, and in excessive self-aggrandizement they went even further.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the brothers were greedy and vulgar, and in building up their own power they went even further.

sentences.zh: 有竇勉潛交巫祝，勉犯法，坐信其詭說，被停官，放歸田園。

translations.literal: There was Dou Mian who secretly associated with shamans; when Mian violated the law, [Xichan] was punished for believing his deceptive talk, stripped of office, and sent back to his estate.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Mian secretly consorted with shamans; when Mian broke the law, Xichan was punished for trusting his deceitful counsel, dismissed from office, and sent home to his estate.

sentences.zh: 尋以尊老，又授開府儀同三司，依舊朝會。

translations.literal: Soon, on account of his senior age, he was again appointed Commissioner with the Same Three Excellencies as an Opening Office, and attended court as before.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, in recognition of his advanced age, he was again granted the rank of commissioner with three-excellency privileges and resumed attendance at court.

sentences.zh: 十三載十二月卒，玄宗哭於行在，贈司徒。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the thirteenth year he died; Xuanzong wept at the temporary palace and posthumously honored him as Grand Mentor.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the twelfth month of the thirteenth year; Xuanzong wept at the imperial camp and posthumously made him grand mentor.

sentences.zh: 財貨鉅萬。

translations.literal: His wealth amounted to tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: His estate was worth tens of thousands of strings of cash.

sentences.zh: 從父弟維鍌，好學，以撰著為業。

translations.literal: His paternal cousin Wei Jian loved learning and made authorship his profession.
translations.idiomatic: His paternal cousin Wei Jian was devoted to learning and made writing his life's work.

sentences.zh: 時宗族咸以外戚，崇飾輿馬，維鍌獨清儉自守。

translations.literal: At the time the clan members all, as affinal kin, adorned their carriages and horses in splendor; Wei Jian alone was frugal and restrained.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the whole clan, as imperial in-laws, decked out their carriages and horses; Wei Jian alone lived plainly and kept himself in check.

sentences.zh: 中書令張說、黃門侍郎盧藏用、給事中裴子餘皆與之親善。

translations.literal: Chief Minister Zhang Yue, Vice Minister of the Yellow Gate Lu Cangyong, and Supervising Secretary Pei Ziyu were all on close terms with him.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Zhang Yue, Vice Minister Lu Cangyong of the Yellow Gate, and Supervising Secretary Pei Ziyu were all close friends of his.

sentences.zh: 官至水部郎中卒。

translations.literal: He reached the office of Director in the Water Bureau and died.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to director in the Water Bureau and died in office.

sentences.zh: 撰《吉凶禮要》二十卷，行於代。

translations.literal: He authored Essentials of Auspicious and Inauspicious Rites in twenty volumes, which circulated in his generation.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Essentials of Auspicious and Inauspicious Rites in twenty volumes, which circulated widely in his day.

sentences.zh: 長孫敞

translations.literal: = Zhangsun Chang =
translations.idiomatic: Zhangsun Chang

sentences.zh: 長孫敞，文德順聖皇后之叔父也。

translations.literal: Zhangsun Chang was the uncle of Empress Wende Shunsheng.
translations.idiomatic: Zhangsun Chang was the uncle of Empress Wende Shunsheng.

sentences.zh: 仕隋為左衛郎將。

translations.literal: He served the Sui as Commandant of the Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Sui he served as commandant of the Left Guard.

sentences.zh: 煬帝幸江都，留敞守京城禁苑。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang visited Jiangdu, he left Chang to guard the imperial park of the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang traveled to Jiangdu, he left Chang to guard the imperial park at the capital.

sentences.zh: 及義旗入關，率子弟迎謁於新豐，從平京城，以功除將作少監。

translations.literal: When the Banner of Righteousness entered the pass, he led his sons and younger relatives to welcome and pay respects at Xinfeng; he followed in pacifying the capital and for his merit was appointed Vice Director of the Directorate of Works.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebel banner entered the pass, he led his sons and kinsmen to greet the new regime at Xinfeng; he took part in pacifying the capital and, for his service, was made vice director of the directorate of works.

sentences.zh: 出為杞州刺史。

translations.literal: He was sent out as prefect of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted as prefect of Qi.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，坐贓免。

translations.literal: Early in the Zhenguan era, he was dismissed for corruption.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhenguan he was dismissed for embezzlement.

sentences.zh: 太宗以后親，常令內給絹以供私費。

translations.literal: Taizong, because he was the empress's kin, regularly had silk supplied from within the palace for his private expenses.
translations.idiomatic: As the empress's relative, he regularly received silk from the inner palace to cover his personal expenses.

sentences.zh: 尋拜宗正少卿，致仕加金紫光祿大夫，累封平原郡公。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Clan; upon retirement he was granted Grand Master of Splendor with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, and cumulatively enfeoffed as Duke of Pingyuan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made vice director of the court of the imperial clan; on retirement he received the rank of grand master of splendor with golden seal and purple ribbon, and was enfeoffed as Duke of Pingyuan.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈幽州都督，謚曰良，陪葬昭陵。

translations.literal: He died; he was posthumously made Area Commander of Youzhou, given the posthumous title Liang (Good), and buried with honor at Zhaoling.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made area commander of Youzhou, given the posthumous name Good (Liang), and buried beside Zhaoling.

sentences.zh: 從父弟　操敞從父弟操，周大司徒、薛國公覽之子也。

translations.literal: Paternal cousin Cao. Chang's paternal cousin Cao was the son of Lan, Grand Minister of Zhou and Duke of Xue state.
translations.idiomatic: Paternal cousin Cao. Zhangsun Chang's paternal cousin Cao was the son of Lan, grand minister of Zhou and Duke of Xue.

sentences.zh: 武德中，為陜東道行臺金部郎中，出為陜州刺史。

translations.literal: In the Wude era he served as Director in the Gold Bureau of the Shaanxi-East Circuit headquarters, then was sent out as prefect of Shaan.
translations.idiomatic: During Wude he served as director in the gold bureau of the Shaanxi-East circuit headquarters, then was posted as prefect of Shaan.

sentences.zh: 自州東引水入城，以代井汲，百姓於今利之。

translations.literal: From east of the prefecture he led water into the city to replace well-drawing; the people benefit from it to this day.
translations.idiomatic: He channeled water from east of the prefecture into the city to replace drawing from wells, and the people still benefit from it today.

sentences.zh: 貞觀中，歷洺州刺史、益揚二州都督府長史，並有善政。

translations.literal: In the Zhenguan era he successively served as prefect of Ming and as chief administrator of the area commands of Yi and Yang, all with good governance.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhenguan he served in turn as prefect of Ming and as chief administrator of the Yi and Yang area commands, earning a reputation for good government in each post.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，以子詮尚太宗女新城公主，拜岐州刺史。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year, because his son Quan married Princess Xincheng, daughter of Taizong, he was appointed prefect of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year, because his son Quan married Taizong's daughter Princess Xincheng, he was appointed prefect of Qi.

sentences.zh: 永徽初，加金紫光祿大夫，賜爵樂壽男。

translations.literal: Early in the Yonghui era he was granted Grand Master of Splendor with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon and enfeoffed as Baron of Leshou.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yonghui he was given the rank of grand master of splendor with golden seal and purple ribbon and enfeoffed as Baron of Leshou.

sentences.zh: 尋卒，贈吏部尚書、并州都督，謚曰安。

translations.literal: Soon he died; he was posthumously made Minister of Personnel and Area Commander of Bingzhou, with the posthumous title An (Peaceful).
translations.idiomatic: He died soon after and was posthumously made minister of personnel and area commander of Bingzhou, with the posthumous name Peaceful (An).

sentences.zh: 詮官至尚書奉御。

translations.literal: Quan reached the office of Palatial Equerry of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Quan rose to palatial equerry of the imperial secretariat.

sentences.zh: 詮即侍中韓瑗妻弟也。

translations.literal: Quan was the younger brother-in-law of Han Yuan, Palace Counselor.
translations.idiomatic: Quan was the younger brother of Palace Counselor Han Yuan's wife.

sentences.zh: 及瑗得罪，事連於詮，減死配流巂州。

translations.literal: When Yuan was convicted, the matter implicated Quan; his death sentence was reduced and he was exiled to Qian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan fell from grace, Quan was implicated; his death sentence was commuted and he was exiled to Qian.

sentences.zh: 詮至流所，縣令希旨杖殺之。

translations.literal: When Quan reached his place of exile, the county magistrate, seeking to curry favor, beat him to death with staves.
translations.idiomatic: When Quan reached his place of exile, the county magistrate, eager to please his superiors, had him beaten to death.

sentences.zh: 趙持滿詮之甥有趙持滿者，工書善射，力搏猛獸，捷及奔馬；

translations.literal: Zhao Chiman. Quan's nephew. There was one Zhao Chiman, skilled at calligraphy and archery, strong enough to wrestle fierce beasts, swift as a galloping horse;
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Chiman, Quan's nephew. There was a man named Zhao Chiman, skilled in calligraphy and archery, strong enough to wrestle wild beasts and quick as a running horse;

sentences.zh: 而親仁愛眾，多所交結，京師無貴賤皆愛慕之。

translations.literal: Yet he was affectionate and benevolent toward the multitude, widely connected; in the capital none, high or low, failed to admire him.
translations.idiomatic: He was warm and generous toward others and had wide connections; in the capital, high and low alike admired him.

sentences.zh: 初為涼州長史，嘗逐野馬，自後射之，無不洞於胸腋，邊人深伏之。

translations.literal: Initially he served as chief administrator of Liang Prefecture; once while chasing wild horses he shot them from behind, none failing to pierce chest and flank; the border people deeply admired him.
translations.idiomatic: He first served as chief administrator of Liang; once, chasing wild horses, he shot them from behind and never failed to pierce chest or flank; the frontier people deeply respected him.

sentences.zh: 許敬宗懼其作難，誣與詮及無忌同反。

translations.literal: Xu Jingzong feared he would cause trouble and falsely charged him with conspiring in rebellion with Quan and Wuji.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Jingzong, fearing he might stir up trouble, falsely accused him of plotting rebellion with Quan and Wuji.

sentences.zh: 及拷訊，終無異詞，且曰：「身可殺，辭不可奪。」

translations.literal: Under interrogation and torture, to the end he made no differing statement, and said: "My person may be killed, but my words cannot be taken away.
translations.idiomatic: Under torture he never changed his story and said, "You may kill my body, but you cannot wrest my confession from me.

sentences.zh: 吏竟代為款以殺之。

translations.literal: The clerks ultimately substituted a confession on his behalf and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: The clerks finally forged a confession in his name and executed him.

sentences.zh: 武承嗣

translations.literal: = Wu Chengsi =
translations.idiomatic: Wu Chengsi

sentences.zh: 武承嗣，荊州都督士矱之孫，則天順聖皇后兄子也。

translations.literal: Wu Chengsi was the grandson of Shi Huo, Area Commander of Jingzhou, and the nephew of Empress Zetian Shunsheng.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Chengsi was grandson of Jingzhou area commander Shi Huo and nephew of Empress Zetian Shunsheng.

sentences.zh: 初，士矱娶相里氏，生元慶、元爽。

translations.literal: Initially Shi Huo married a woman of the Xiangli clan and begot Yuanshi and Yuanshuang.
translations.idiomatic: At first Shi Huo married a woman of the Xiangli clan and had Yuanshi and Yuanshuang.

sentences.zh: 又娶楊氏，生三女：長適越王府功曹賀蘭越石，次則天，次適郭氏。

translations.literal: He also married a woman of the Yang clan and begot three daughters: the eldest married Helan Yueshi, registrar of the Prince of Yue's household; the second was Zetian; the third married into the Guo clan.
translations.idiomatic: He also married a woman of the Yang clan and had three daughters: the eldest married Helan Yueshi, registrar in the household of the Prince of Yue; the second was Zetian; the third married into the Guo clan.

sentences.zh: 士矱卒後，兄子惟良、懷運及元爽等遇楊氏失禮。

translations.literal: After Shi Huo died, his brother's sons Weiliang and Huaiyun, together with Yuanshuang and the others, treated Lady Yang without proper courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: After Shi Huo died, his brother's sons Weiliang and Huaiyun, along with Yuanshuang and the others, treated Lady Yang discourteously.

sentences.zh: 及則天立為皇后，追贈士矱為司徒、周忠孝王，封楊氏代國夫人。

translations.literal: When Zetian was established as empress, Shi Huo was posthumously honored as Minister of Works and Loyal and Filial King of Zhou; Lady Yang was enfeoffed as Lady of Dai state.
translations.idiomatic: When Zetian became empress, Shi Huo was posthumously made minister of works and Loyal and Filial King of Zhou, and Lady Yang was enfeoffed as Lady of Dai.

sentences.zh: 賀蘭越石早卒，封其妻為韓國夫人。

translations.literal: Helan Yueshi died early; his wife was enfeoffed as Lady of Han state.
translations.idiomatic: Helan Yueshi died young, and his wife was enfeoffed as Lady of Han.

sentences.zh: 尋又加贈士矱為太尉，楊氏改封為榮國夫人。

translations.literal: Soon Shi Huo was further posthumously honored as Grand Marshal, and Lady Yang was re-enfeoffed as Lady Rongguo.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Shi Huo was further honored as grand marshal, and Lady Yang was re-enfeoffed as Lady Rongguo.

sentences.zh: 時元慶仕為宗正少卿，元爽為少府少監，惟良為衛尉少卿。

translations.literal: At the time Yuanshi served as Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Clan, Yuanshuang as Vice Director of the Palace Handicrafts Office, and Weiliang as Vice Director of the Minister of the Guard.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Yuanshi was vice director of the court of the imperial clan, Yuanshuang was vice director of the palace handicrafts office, and Weiliang was vice director of the guard.

sentences.zh: 榮國夫人恨其疇日薄己，諷皇后抗疏請出元慶等為外職，佯為退讓，其實惡之也。

translations.literal: Lady Rongguo resented their past slight toward her; she prompted the empress to submit a forthright memorial requesting that Yuanshi and the others be sent to outside posts, feigning deference — in truth she detested them.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Rongguo resented the way they had once treated her; she urged the empress to submit a bold memorial asking that Yuanshi and the others be sent to provincial posts, pretending humility while in fact loathing them.

sentences.zh: 於是元慶為龍州刺史，元爽為濠州刺史，惟良為始州刺史。

translations.literal: Thereupon Yuanshi became prefect of Long, Yuanshuang prefect of Hao, and Weiliang prefect of Shi.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Yuanshi was made prefect of Long, Yuanshuang prefect of Hao, and Weiliang prefect of Shi.

sentences.zh: 元慶至州病卒，元爽自濠州又配流振州而死。

translations.literal: Yuanshi reached his prefecture and died of illness; Yuanshuang from Hao was further exiled to Zhen and died there.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanshi reached his prefecture and died of illness; Yuanshuang was exiled from Hao to Zhen and died there.

sentences.zh: 乾封年，惟良與弟淄州刺史懷運，以嶽牧例集於泰山之下。

translations.literal: In the Qianfeng era, Weiliang and his brother Huaiyun, prefect of Zi, gathered at the foot of Mount Tai according to the precedent for area commanders.
translations.idiomatic: In the Qianfeng era, Weiliang and his brother Huaiyun, prefect of Zi, assembled at the foot of Mount Tai according to the custom for frontier governors.

sentences.zh: 時韓國夫人女賀蘭氏在宮中，頗承恩寵。

translations.literal: At the time the daughter of Lady of Han, of the Helan clan, was in the palace and enjoyed considerable favor.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the daughter of Lady of Han, a Helan, was in the palace and enjoyed considerable favor.

sentences.zh: 則天意欲除之，諷高宗幸其母宅，因惟良等獻食，則天密令人以毒藥貯賀蘭氏食中，賀蘭氏食之，暴卒，歸罪於惟良、懷運，乃誅之。

translations.literal: Zetian wished to eliminate them; she prompted Gaozong to visit her mother's house, and when Weiliang and the others presented food, Zetian secretly had someone place poison in Lady Helan's food; Lady Helan ate it and died suddenly; blame was placed on Weiliang and Huaiyun, and they were executed.
translations.idiomatic: Zetian intended to destroy them; she induced Gaozong to visit her mother's house, and when Weiliang and the others presented food, she secretly had poison placed in Lady Helan's portion; Lady Helan ate and died suddenly; the blame was laid on Weiliang and Huaiyun, and they were put to death.

sentences.zh: 仍諷百僚抗表請改其姓為蝮氏，絕其屬籍。

translations.literal: She also prompted the hundred officials to submit forthright memorials requesting that their surname be changed to Fu (Viper) and their clan registry be severed.
translations.idiomatic: She also urged the officials to submit bold memorials asking that their surname be changed to Viper and their clan registry cut off.

sentences.zh: 元爽等緣坐配流嶺外而死，乃以韓國夫人之子敏之為士矱嗣，改姓武氏，累拜左侍極、蘭臺太史，襲爵周國公。

translations.literal: Yuanshuang and the others, implicated by association, were exiled beyond the Ling mountains and died; then Minzhi, son of Lady of Han, was made heir of Shi Huo, his surname changed to Wu; he was repeatedly promoted to Left Palace Attendant and Grand Astrologer of the Orchid Terrace, and inherited the dukedom of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanshuang and the others were implicated, exiled beyond the mountains, and died; then Minzhi, son of Lady of Han, was made Shi Huo's heir, took the surname Wu, rose to left palace attendant and grand astrologer of the Orchid Terrace, and inherited the dukedom of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 仍令鳩集學士李嗣真、吳兢之徒，於蘭臺刊正經史，並著撰傳記。

translations.literal: He was also ordered to gather scholars such as Li Sizhen and Wu Jing at the Orchid Terrace to edit and correct the classics and histories, and to compose biographies and annals.
translations.idiomatic: He was also ordered to assemble scholars such as Li Sizhen and Wu Jing at the Orchid Terrace to revise the classics and histories and to write biographies and chronicles.

sentences.zh: 敏之既年少色美，烝於榮國夫人，恃寵多愆犯，則天頗不悅之，

translations.literal: Minzhi was young and handsome; he committed incest with Lady Rongguo; relying on favor he repeatedly transgressed, and Zetian was quite displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Minzhi was young and handsome; he had an affair with Lady Rongguo; trusting in favor, he repeatedly overstepped, and Zetian grew deeply displeased.

sentences.zh: 榮國夫人卒，則天出內大瑞錦，令敏之造佛像追福，敏之自隱用之。

translations.literal: When Lady Rongguo died, Zetian brought out great auspicious brocade from the inner palace and ordered Minzhi to have a Buddhist image made for merit; Minzhi secretly kept it for himself.
translations.idiomatic: When Lady Rongguo died, Zetian brought out precious brocade from the inner palace and ordered Minzhi to commission a Buddhist image for her merit; Minzhi kept it for himself instead.

sentences.zh: 又司衛少卿楊思儉女有殊色，高宗及則天自選以為太子妃，成有定日矣，敏之又逼而淫焉。

translations.literal: Moreover the daughter of Yang Sijian, Vice Director of the Chamberlain for the Palace Revenues, was of exceptional beauty; Gaozong and Zetian personally selected her as crown princess — the date was already set — yet Minzhi forced and violated her.
translations.idiomatic: The daughter of Vice Director Yang Sijian of the palace revenues was exceptionally beautiful; Gaozong and Zetian had personally chosen her as crown princess and even set the wedding date, yet Minzhi forced himself on her.

sentences.zh: 及在榮國服內，私釋衰绖，著吉服，奏妓樂。

translations.literal: While in mourning for Lady Rongguo, he privately cast off his hemp mourning garments, wore festive dress, and played music with singing girls.
translations.idiomatic: During mourning for Lady Rongguo, he privately cast off his mourning clothes, put on festive dress, and entertained himself with music and dancing girls.

sentences.zh: 時太平公主尚幼，往來榮國之家，宮人侍行，又嘗為敏之所逼。

translations.literal: At the time Princess Taiping was still young; going to and from Lady Rongguo's house with palace women attending, she too was once forced by Minzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Taiping was still young then; when she visited Lady Rongguo's house with palace women in attendance, she too was once assaulted by Minzhi.

sentences.zh: 俄而奸汙事發，配流雷州，行至韶州，以馬韁自縊而死。

translations.literal: Soon the affair of debauchery broke out; he was exiled to Lei; on the road at Shao he hanged himself with a horse bridle.
translations.idiomatic: Before long his crimes of debauchery came to light; he was exiled to Lei, and on the road at Shao he hanged himself with a horse bridle.

sentences.zh: 承嗣，元爽子也。

translations.literal: Chengsi was Yuanshuang's son.
translations.idiomatic: Chengsi was Yuanshuang's son.

sentences.zh: 敏之死後，自嶺南召還，拜尚衣奉御，襲祖爵周國公。

translations.literal: After Minzhi's death, he was recalled from Lingnan, appointed Palatial Equerry of the Imperial Wardrobe, and inherited his grandfather's dukedom of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Minzhi's death he was recalled from the far south, appointed palatial equerry of the imperial wardrobe, and inherited his grandfather's dukedom of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 俄遷秘書監。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to Director of the Imperial Library.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to director of the imperial library.

sentences.zh: 則天臨朝，追尊士矱為忠孝太皇，置崇先府官屬，五代祖已下，皆為王。

translations.literal: When Zetian assumed the regency, Shi Huo was posthumously honored as the Loyal and Filial Grand Emperor; the Chongxian Office and its staff were established; from the fifth-generation ancestor down, all were made kings.
translations.idiomatic: When Zetian took the throne, Shi Huo was posthumously honored as the Loyal and Filial Grand Emperor; the Chongxian Office and its staff were established, and from the fifth-generation ancestor downward all were made kings.

sentences.zh: 嗣聖元年，以承嗣為禮部尚書。

translations.literal: In the first year of Sisheng, Chengsi was appointed Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Sisheng, Chengsi was appointed minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 尋除太常卿、同中書門下三品。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Minister of Ceremonials and Same Rank as the Three Departments of the Secretariat and Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made minister of ceremonials with rank equal to the three top ministers.

sentences.zh: 垂拱中，轉春官尚書，依舊知政事，

translations.literal: In the Chuigong era he was transferred to Minister of Personnel and continued to manage state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: During Chuigong he was transferred to minister of personnel and continued to manage state affairs.

sentences.zh: 代蘇良嗣為文昌左相、同鳳閣鸞臺三品，兼知內史事，

translations.literal: He replaced Su Liangsi as Left Minister of the Hall of Literary Glory, Same Rank as the Three Departments of the Phoenix Pavilion and Orchid Terrace, concurrently managing Secretariat affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He replaced Su Liangsi as left minister of the Hall of Literary Glory with rank equal to the three top ministers, and concurrently managed secretariat affairs.

sentences.zh: 於東都創置武氏七廟，追尊周文王為始祖文皇帝，王子武為睿祖康皇帝，云武氏之先也。

translations.literal: At the eastern capital he newly established the seven temples of the Wu clan; King Wen of Zhou was posthumously honored as Founding Ancestor and Literary Emperor, and Prince Wu as Sagacious Ancestor and Princely Emperor — said to be the ancestors of the Wu clan.
translations.idiomatic: At the eastern capital he established seven ancestral temples for the Wu clan, posthumously honoring King Wen of Zhou as Founding Ancestor and Literary Emperor and Prince Wu as Sagacious Ancestor and Princely Emperor, claiming them as forebears of the Wu house.

sentences.zh: 后五代祖贈太原靖王居常為嚴祖成皇帝，高祖贈趙肅恭王克己為肅祖章敬皇帝，曾祖贈魏康王儉為烈祖昭安皇帝，祖贈周安成王華為顯祖文穆皇帝，考忠孝太皇為太祖孝明高皇帝，妣皆隨帝號曰皇后。

translations.literal: The empress's fifth-generation ancestor, posthumously King Jing of Taiyuan Juchang, was made Stern Ancestor and Accomplished Emperor; the high ancestor, posthumously King Su and Gong of Zhao Keji, was made Reverent Ancestor and Manifestly Respectful Emperor; the great-great-grandfather, posthumously King Kang of Wei Jian, was made Glorious Ancestor and Illustrious Peaceful Emperor; the grandfather, posthumously King Ancheng of Zhou Hua, was made Prominent Ancestor and Literary and Solemn Emperor; the father, the Loyal and Filial Grand Emperor, was made Great Ancestor and Filial and Illustrious High Emperor; their wives all followed the imperial titles and were called empresses.
translations.idiomatic: The empress's fifth-generation ancestor Juchang, posthumously King Jing of Taiyuan, was made Stern Ancestor and Accomplished Emperor; high ancestor Keji, posthumously King Su and Gong of Zhao, was made Reverent Ancestor and Manifestly Respectful Emperor; great-great-grandfather Jian, posthumously King Kang of Wei, was made Glorious Ancestor and Illustrious Peaceful Emperor; grandfather Hua, posthumously King Ancheng of Zhou, was made Prominent Ancestor and Literary and Solemn Emperor; father the Loyal and Filial Grand Emperor was made Great Ancestor and Filial and Illustrious High Emperor; and each man's wife received a matching empress title.

sentences.zh: 元慶為梁憲王，元爽為魏德王。

translations.literal: Yuanshi was made King Liangxian, and Yuanshuang King Weide.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanshi was made Prince Liangxian, and Yuanshuang Prince Weide.

sentences.zh: 又追封伯父及兄弟俱為王，諸姑姊為長公主。

translations.literal: Paternal uncles and brothers were also posthumously enfeoffed as kings, and aunts and elder sisters as grand princesses.
translations.idiomatic: Paternal uncles and brothers were also posthumously made princes, and aunts and elder sisters were made grand princesses.

sentences.zh: 於是封承嗣為魏王，元慶子夏官尚書三思為梁王，后從父兄子納言攸寧為建昌王，太子通事舍人攸歸為九江王，司禮卿重規為高平王，左衛親府中郎將載德為潁川王，右衛將軍攸暨為千乘王，司農卿懿宗為河內王，左千牛中郎將嗣宗為臨川王，右衛勛二府中郎將攸宜為建安王，尚乘直長攸望為會稽王，太子通事舍人攸緒為安平王，攸止為恆安王。

translations.literal: Thereupon Chengsi was enfeoffed as King of Wei; Yuanshi's son Sansi, Minister of Personnel, as King of Liang; the empress's paternal cousin's son Youning, Censor-in-Chief, as King of Jianchang; Yougui, Attendant of the Heir Apparent's Communications, as King of Jiujiang; Chonggui, Minister of Rites, as King of Gaoping; Zaidé, Captain in the Left Guard's Household Guards, as King of Yingchuan; Youji, General of the Right Guard, as King of Qiansheng; Yizong, Minister of Revenue, as King of Henan; Sizong, Captain of the Left Imperial Stables, as King of Linchuan; Youyi, Captain in the Right Guard's Meritorious Service Office, as King of Jian'an; Youwang, Chief Steward of the Imperial Stud, as King of Kuaiji; Youxu, Attendant of the Heir Apparent's Communications, as King of Anping; and Youzhi as King of Heng'an.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Chengsi was made Prince of Wei; Yuanshi's son Sansi, minister of personnel, was made Prince of Liang; the empress's paternal cousin's son Youning, censor-in-chief, was made Prince of Jianchang; Yougui, attendant of the heir apparent's communications, was made Prince of Jiujiang; Chonggui, minister of rites, was made Prince of Gaoping; Zaidé, captain in the Left Guard household guards, was made Prince of Yingchuan; Youji, general of the Right Guard, was made Prince of Qiansheng; Yizong, minister of revenue, was made Prince of Henan; Sizong, captain of the Left Imperial Stables, was made Prince of Linchuan; Youyi, captain in the Right Guard meritorious service office, was made Prince of Jian'an; Youwang, chief steward of the imperial stud, was made Prince of Kuaiji; Youxu, attendant of the heir apparent's communications, was made Prince of Anping; and Youzhi was made Prince of Heng'an.

sentences.zh: 又封承嗣男延基為南陽王，延秀為淮陽王，三思男崇訓為高陽王，崇烈為新安王，后兄子贈陳王承業男延暉為嗣陳王，延祚為咸安王。

translations.literal: Chengsi's sons Yanji and Yanxiu were also enfeoffed as King of Nanyang and King of Huaiyang; Sansi's sons Chongxun and Chonglie as King of Gaoyang and King of Xin'an; and the empress's brother's son, posthumously King of Chen Chengye's son Yanhui, as Heir King of Chen, and Yanzuo as King of Xian'an.
translations.idiomatic: Chengsi's sons Yanji and Yanxiu were also made Prince of Nanyang and Prince of Huaiyang; Sansi's sons Chongxun and Chonglie were made Prince of Gaoyang and Prince of Xin'an; and the empress's brother's son, posthumously Prince of Chen Chengye's son Yanhui, was made Heir Prince of Chen, and Yanzuo was made Prince of Xian'an.

sentences.zh: 承嗣嘗諷則天革命，盡誅皇室諸王及公卿中不附己者，承嗣從父弟三思又盛贊其計，天下於今冤之。

translations.literal: Chengsi once urged Zetian to change the dynasty, executing all imperial princes and among the high ministers those who did not attach to him; his paternal cousin Sansi greatly praised the plan — the world to this day holds it a grievous wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Chengsi once urged Zetian to seize the throne and execute every imperial prince and every high minister who would not support him; his paternal cousin Sansi strongly endorsed the plan — to this day the realm considers it a great injustice.

sentences.zh: 俄又賜承嗣實封千戶，仍監修國史。

translations.literal: Soon Chengsi was granted a taxable fief of one thousand households and continued to supervise compilation of the national history.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Chengsi was granted a taxable fief of one thousand households and was put in charge of compiling the national history.

sentences.zh: 承嗣自為次當為皇儲，令鳳閣舍人張嘉福諷諭百姓抗表陳請，則天竟不許，

translations.literal: Chengsi regarded himself as next in line to be crown heir; he had Zhang Jiafu, Drafting Attendant of the Phoenix Pavilion, urge the people to submit forthright memorials petitioning for it — Zetian ultimately did not consent.
translations.idiomatic: Chengsi believed he should be next in line for the throne; he had Drafting Attendant Zhang Jiafu of the Phoenix Pavilion incite the people to submit petitions on his behalf — but Zetian refused.

sentences.zh: 授特進。

translations.literal: He was granted Special Advancement.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted the rank of special advancement.

sentences.zh: 尋拜太子太保，罷知政事。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent and dismissed from managing state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made grand tutor of the heir apparent and removed from managing state affairs.

sentences.zh: 承嗣以不得立為皇太子，怏怏而卒，贈太尉、并州牧，謚曰宣。

translations.literal: Chengsi, because he could not be established as crown prince, died in resentment; he was posthumously made Grand Marshal and Governor of Bingzhou, with the posthumous title Xuan (Proclaiming).
translations.idiomatic: Chengsi, bitter that he was never made crown prince, died in resentment; he was posthumously made grand marshal and governor of Bingzhou, with the posthumous name Proclaiming (Xuan).

sentences.zh: 子延基襲爵，則天避其父名，封為繼魏王。

translations.literal: His son Yanji inherited the enfeoffment; Zetian avoided his father's name and enfeoffed him as Succession King of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yanji inherited the title; to avoid his father's name, Zetian enfeoffed him as Heir Prince of Wei.

sentences.zh: 尋與其妻永泰郡主及懿德太子等，話及張易之兄弟出入宮中，恐有不利，後忿爭不協，泄之，則天聞而大怒，咸令自殺。

translations.literal: Soon he, with his wife the Princess of Yongtai Commandery and Crown Prince Yide and others, discussed the Zhang Yizhi brothers entering and leaving the palace and feared harm; later in angry quarrel they fell out and leaked it; Zetian heard and was greatly angered; all were ordered to kill themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he, his wife the Princess of Yongtai, Crown Prince Yide, and others discussed the Zhang Yizhi brothers' comings and goings in the palace and feared trouble; later, after an angry quarrel, the matter was leaked; when Zetian heard of it she was furious and ordered them all to take their own lives.

sentences.zh: 復以承嗣次子延義為繼魏王。

translations.literal: Chengsi's second son Yanyi was again made Succession King of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Chengsi's second son Yanyi was then made Heir Prince of Wei.

sentences.zh: 中宗即位，侍中敬暉等以唐室中興，武氏諸王宜削其王爵，乃率群官上表曰：

translations.literal: When Zhongzong took the throne, Palace Counselor Jing Hui and others, because the Tang house had been restored, held that the Wu princes should be stripped of their princely ranks; they led the officials in submitting a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: When Zhongzong ascended the throne, Palace Counselor Jing Hui and others, holding that the Tang restoration required stripping the Wu princes of their royal titles, led the officials in submitting a memorial that read:

sentences.zh: 中書舍人岑義之詞也。

translations.literal: These were the words of Cen Yi, Drafting Attendant of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was drafted by Secretariat Attendant Cen Yi.

sentences.zh: 上答曰：

translations.literal: The emperor replied:
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied:

sentences.zh: 於是降封梁王三思為德靜郡王，量減實封二百戶，定王、駙馬都尉攸暨為樂壽郡王，河內郡王懿宗為耿國公，建昌郡王攸寧為江國公，會稽郡王攸望為鄴國公，臨川郡王嗣宗為管國公，建安郡王攸宜為息國公，高平郡王重規為鄶國公，繼魏王延義為魏國公，安平郡王攸緒為巢國公，高陽郡王、駙馬都尉崇訓為酆國公，淮陽郡王延秀為桓國公，咸安郡王延祚為咸安郡公。

translations.literal: Thereupon Prince of Liang Sansi was demoted and enfeoffed as Duke of Dejing Commandery, with his taxable fief reduced by two hundred households; Prince of Ding and Commandant of the Imperial Stud Youji as Duke of Leshou Commandery; Duke of Henan Commandery Yizong as Duke of Geng state; Duke of Jianchang Commandery Youning as Duke of Jiang state; Duke of Kuaiji Commandery Youwang as Duke of Ye state; Duke of Linchuan Commandery Sizong as Duke of Guan state; Duke of Jian'an Commandery Youyi as Duke of Xi state; Duke of Gaoping Commandery Chonggui as Duke of Kuai state; Succession Prince of Wei Yanyi as Duke of Wei state; Duke of Anping Commandery Youxu as Duke of Chao state; Duke of Gaoyang Commandery and Commandant of the Imperial Stud Chongxun as Duke of Feng state; Duke of Huaiyang Commandery Yanxiu as Duke of Huan state; and Duke of Xian'an Commandery Yanzuo as Duke of Xian'an Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Prince of Liang Sansi was demoted to Duke of Dejing, with his taxable fief reduced by two hundred households; Prince of Ding and imperial stud commandant Youji was made Duke of Leshou; Duke of Henan Yizong was made Duke of Geng; Duke of Jianchang Youning was made Duke of Jiang; Duke of Kuaiji Youwang was made Duke of Ye; Duke of Linchuan Sizong was made Duke of Guan; Duke of Jian'an Youyi was made Duke of Xi; Duke of Gaoping Chonggui was made Duke of Kuai; Heir Prince of Wei Yanyi was made Duke of Wei; Duke of Anping Youxu was made Duke of Chao; Duke of Gaoyang and imperial stud commandant Chongxun was made Duke of Feng; Duke of Huaiyang Yanxiu was made Duke of Huan; and Duke of Xian'an Yanzuo was made Duke of Xian'an.

sentences.zh: 中宗時，嗣宗至曹州刺史，攸宜工部尚書，重規岐州刺史，相次病卒。

translations.literal: In Zhongzong's time, Sizong reached prefect of Cao; Youyi, Minister of Works; Chonggui, prefect of Qi — they successively died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhongzong, Sizong rose to prefect of Cao, Youyi to minister of works, and Chonggui to prefect of Qi; they died of illness in succession.

sentences.zh: 攸望至太常卿，左遷春州司馬而死。

translations.literal: Youwang reached Minister of Ceremonials, was demoted and transferred as military aide of Chun Prefecture, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Youwang rose to minister of ceremonials, was demoted to military aide of Chun, and died there.

sentences.zh: 延秀伏誅後，武氏宗屬緣坐誅死及配流，殆將盡矣，

translations.literal: After Yanxiu was executed, Wu clansmen by implication were put to death or exiled — nearly all were gone.
translations.idiomatic: After Yanxiu was executed, Wu clansmen implicated in his case were killed or exiled until almost none remained.

sentences.zh: 制削士彟帝號，依舊追贈太原王，妻楊氏亦削后號，依舊為太原王妃。

translations.literal: An edict stripped Shi Huo of his imperial title; he was posthumously honored as before as King of Taiyuan; his wife Lady Yang also had her empress title stripped and was as before Lady of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: An edict stripped Shi Huo of his imperial title and restored his posthumous rank as King of Taiyuan; his wife Lady Yang also lost her empress title and was again styled Lady of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 承嗣子　延秀延秀，承嗣第二子也。

translations.literal: Chengsi's son Yanxiu. Yanxiu was Chengsi's second son.
translations.idiomatic: Chengsi's son Yanxiu. Yanxiu was Chengsi's second son.

sentences.zh: 則天時，突厥默啜上言有女請和親，制延秀與閻知微俱往突厥，將親迎默啜女為妻。

translations.literal: In Zetian's time, Mochuo of the Turks reported that he had a daughter and requested a marriage alliance; Yanxiu was ordered to go with Yan Zhiwei to the Turks to personally welcome Mochuo's daughter as wife.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zetian, the Turkic ruler Mochuo reported that he had a daughter and sought a marriage alliance; Yanxiu was ordered to go with Yan Zhiwei to the Turks to fetch Mochuo's daughter as his bride.

sentences.zh: 既而默啜執知微，入冠趙、定等州，故延秀久不得還。

translations.literal: Soon Mochuo seized Zhiwei and invaded Zhao, Ding, and other prefectures; therefore Yanxiu long could not return.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Mochuo seized Zhiwei and invaded Zhao, Ding, and other prefectures, so Yanxiu was unable to return for a long time.

sentences.zh: 神龍初，默啜更請通和，先令延秀送款，始得歸，封桓國公，又授左衛中郎將。

translations.literal: Early in Shenlong, Mochuo again requested reconciliation; he first had Yanxiu deliver a pledge of allegiance; only then was Yanxiu able to return; he was enfeoffed as Duke of Huan state and also appointed Captain in the Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Shenlong era, Mochuo again sought peace and first required Yanxiu to deliver a pledge of submission; only then was Yanxiu allowed to return; he was enfeoffed as Duke of Huan and appointed captain in the Left Guard.

sentences.zh: 時武崇訓為安樂公主婿，即延秀從父兄，數引至主第。

translations.literal: At the time Wu Chongxun was son-in-law to Princess Anle — he was Yanxiu's paternal cousin — and repeatedly brought him to the princess's residence.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Wu Chongxun was married to Princess Anle; as Yanxiu's paternal cousin, he often brought Yanxiu to the princess's residence.

sentences.zh: 延秀久在蕃中，解突厥語，常於主第，延秀唱突厥歌，作胡旋舞，有姿媚，主甚喜之。

translations.literal: Yanxiu had long been among the barbarians, understood Turkic speech; often at the princess's residence Yanxiu would sing Turkic songs and perform the Hu Xuan dance; he had charm and grace; the princess greatly favored him.
translations.idiomatic: Yanxiu had spent years among the Turks and knew their language; at the princess's residence he would sing Turkic songs and perform the whirling Hu dance with seductive grace, and the princess doted on him.

sentences.zh: 及崇訓死，延秀得幸，遂尚公主。

translations.literal: When Chongxun died, Yanxiu gained favor and thereupon married the princess.
translations.idiomatic: After Chongxun died, Yanxiu won the princess's favor and married her.

sentences.zh: 主，韋后所生男女中最小。

translations.literal: The princess was the youngest of the sons and daughters born to Empress Wei.
translations.idiomatic: The princess was the youngest child born to Empress Wei.

sentences.zh: 初，中宗遷於房州，欲達州境，生於路次。

translations.literal: Initially, when Zhongzong was relocated to Fang Prefecture, just as he was about to reach the prefectural border, she was born on the road.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhongzong was first sent into exile at Fang Prefecture, she was born on the road before he even reached the border.

sentences.zh: 性惠敏，容質秀絕。

translations.literal: By nature intelligent and quick; her appearance was surpassingly beautiful.
translations.idiomatic: She was clever by nature and possessed extraordinary beauty.

sentences.zh: 中宗、韋后愛龐日深，恣其所欲，奏請無不允許。

translations.literal: Zhongzong and Empress Wei loved and indulged her daily more deeply; they indulged all her desires; whatever she memorialized was never denied.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzong and Empress Wei grew ever more devoted to her, granting her every wish; no petition she submitted was ever refused.

sentences.zh: 恃寵橫縱，權傾天下，自王侯宰相已下，除拜多出其門。

translations.literal: Relying on favor she acted with arrogance and impunity; her power eclipsed the realm; from kings, marquises, and chancellors downward, most appointments came from her household.
translations.idiomatic: Drunk on imperial favor, she acted with reckless arrogance; her influence overshadowed the empire, and from princes and chancellors on down, most appointments issued from her door.

sentences.zh: 所營第宅並造安樂佛寺，擬於宮掖，巧妙過之。

translations.literal: The residences and estates she built, and the Anle Buddhist Temple she constructed, rivaled the palace precincts in design and surpassed them in ingenuity.
translations.idiomatic: The mansions she built and the Anle Buddhist Temple she erected were modeled on the palace itself—and surpassed it in craftsmanship.

sentences.zh: 令楊務廉於城西造定昆池於其莊，延袤數里。

translations.literal: She had Yang Wulian build the Dingkun Pond at her estate west of the city, extending several li.
translations.idiomatic: She had Yang Wulian construct the Dingkun Pond at her manor west of the capital, a lake stretching several li.

sentences.zh: 出降之時，以皇后仗發於宮中，中宗與韋后御安福門觀之，燈燭供擬，徹明如晝。

translations.literal: When she went forth to marry, the empress's ceremonial guard was dispatched from within the palace; Zhongzong and Empress Wei mounted the Anfu Gate to observe; lamps and candles were laid out so that it was bright as day.
translations.idiomatic: For her wedding procession, the empress's honor guard marched out from the palace; Zhongzong and Empress Wei watched from the Anfu Gate as lanterns and candles lit the scene bright as noon.

sentences.zh: 延秀拜度日，授太常卿，兼右衛將軍、駙馬都尉，改封恆國公，實封五百戶。

translations.literal: After Yanxiu's wedding ceremony, he was appointed Minister of Ceremonies, concurrently General of the Right Guard and Commandant of Horsemen for the Imperial Son-in-Law; his fief was changed to Duke of Heng State with a taxable fief of five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: After the wedding rites, Yanxiu was made Minister of Ceremonies, concurrently general of the Right Guard and imperial son-in-law commandant; his title was changed to Duke of Heng with a taxable fief of five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 廢休祥宅，於金城坊造宅，窮極壯麗，帑藏為之空竭。

translations.literal: The Xiuxiang residence was demolished and a mansion was built in Jincheng Ward, extravagantly magnificent to the utmost; the treasury was emptied on its account.
translations.idiomatic: The Xiuxiang mansion was torn down and a new residence built in Jincheng Ward of breathtaking extravagance, draining the treasury dry.

sentences.zh: 崇訓子數歲，因加金紫光祿大夫、太常卿同正員、左衛將軍，封鎬國公，賜實封五百戶，以嗣其父。

translations.literal: Chongxun's son, only a few years old, was accordingly promoted to Grand Master of the Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon, Senior Advisor to the Minister of Ceremonies with full salary, General of the Left Guard, enfeoffed as Duke of Hao State with a taxable fief of five hundred households, to succeed his father.
translations.idiomatic: Chongxun's son, only a few years old, was promoted to grand master of the gold seal and purple ribbon, senior advisor to the minister of ceremonies with full salary, general of the Left Guard, and enfeoffed as Duke of Hao with five hundred taxable households to succeed his father.

sentences.zh: 公主產男滿月，中宗、韋后幸其第，就第放赦，遣宰臣李嶠、文士宋之問、沈佺期、張說、閻朝隱等數百人賦詩美之。

translations.literal: When the princess's male child reached the full month, Zhongzong and Empress Wei visited her residence, granted an amnesty at the residence, and dispatched several hundred chancellors and literary men including Li Qiao, Song Zhiwen, Shen Quanqi, Zhang Yue, and Yan Chaoyin to compose poetry praising the occasion.
translations.idiomatic: When the princess's son completed his first month, Zhongzong and Empress Wei visited her home, proclaimed an amnesty on the spot, and sent several hundred court ministers and poets—including Li Qiao, Song Zhiwen, Shen Quanqi, Zhang Yue, and Yan Chaoyin—to write celebratory verses.

sentences.zh: 延秀既恃恩，放縱無所忌憚。

translations.literal: Now that Yanxiu relied on imperial favor, he indulged himself without restraint or fear.
translations.idiomatic: Emboldened by imperial favor, Yanxiu gave himself over to unrestrained excess without a trace of fear.

sentences.zh: 又公主府倉曹符鳳知延秀有不臣之心，遂說曰：「今天下蒼生，猶以武氏為念，大周必可再興。

translations.literal: Moreover Fu Feng, Warehouse Clerk of the princess's household, knowing Yanxiu harbored disloyal ambitions, thereupon persuaded him, saying: "Today the people of the realm still look to the Wu clan; the Great Zhou can surely rise again.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Feng, a warehouse clerk in the princess's household, sensed Yanxiu's disloyal ambitions and urged him: "The people still yearn for the Wu clan—the Great Zhou can rise again.

sentences.zh: 按讖書云『黑衣神孫披天裳』，駙馬即神皇之孫也。」

translations.literal: According to prophetic texts it says, 'The divine grandson in black robes spreads the celestial garment' — the imperial son-in-law is precisely the divine emperor's grandson."
translations.idiomatic: Prophetic texts say, 'The divine grandson in black spreads the heavenly robe'—and you, the imperial son-in-law, are that divine emperor's grandson."

sentences.zh: 每勸令著皁襖子以應之。

translations.literal: He continually urged him to wear black jackets to conform to the prophecy.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly urged Yanxiu to wear black jackets to fulfill the prophecy.

sentences.zh: 及韋庶人敗，延秀與公主在內宅，格戰良久。

translations.literal: When Empress Wei the commoner was overthrown, Yanxiu and the princess were in the inner residence, fighting in close combat for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Wei fell, Yanxiu and the princess barricaded themselves in the inner quarters and fought a prolonged hand-to-hand battle.

sentences.zh: 皆斬之。

translations.literal: Both were beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Both were beheaded.

sentences.zh: 後追貶為悖逆庶人。

translations.literal: Later she was posthumously demoted as a rebellious commoner.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward she was posthumously stripped of rank and condemned as a treasonous commoner.

sentences.zh: 元慶子　三思三思，元慶子也。

translations.literal: Yuanshi's son Sansi. Sansi was Yuanshi's son.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanshi's son Sansi. Sansi was Yuanshi's son.

sentences.zh: 少以后族累轉右衛將軍。

translations.literal: In youth, through empress-kin connections he was transferred repeatedly, becoming General of the Right Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth he rose through empress-kin connections to become general of the Right Guard.

sentences.zh: 則天臨朝，擢拜夏官尚書。

translations.literal: When Zetian held court, he was promoted and appointed Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: When Zetian took power, he was promoted to minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 及革命，封梁王，賜實封一千戶。

translations.literal: When the dynasty was changed, he was enfeoffed as King of Liang with a taxable fief of one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: At the founding of her new dynasty, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Liang with a taxable fief of one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 尋拜天官尚書，

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Minister of the Interior.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed minister of the interior.

sentences.zh: 轉春官尚書，監修國史，

translations.literal: He was transferred to Minister of Rites and supervised compilation of the national history.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to minister of rites and put in charge of compiling the national history.

sentences.zh: 檢校內史。

translations.literal: He served as acting Secretary of the Interior.
translations.idiomatic: He served as acting secretary of the interior.

sentences.zh: 二年，進拜特進、太子賓客，仍並依舊監修國史。

translations.literal: In the second year he was promoted to Special Advancement and Mentor to the Heir Apparent, and still continued to supervise compilation of the national history as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was promoted to special advancement and mentor to the heir apparent, while continuing to oversee the national history as before.
