sentences.zh: 三思略涉文史，性傾巧便僻，善事人，由是特蒙信任。

translations.literal: Sansi had some exposure to literature and history; by nature he was inclined to cleverness and unorthodox expedients, skilled at pleasing people — thereby he was especially entrusted.
translations.idiomatic: Sansi had a modest literary education and a gift for clever, unscrupulous flattery; he knew how to win people over and thereby earned extraordinary trust.

sentences.zh: 則天數幸其第，賞賜甚厚。

translations.literal: Zetian frequently visited his residence and bestowed exceedingly generous rewards.
translations.idiomatic: Zetian visited his home again and again and showered him with lavish gifts.

sentences.zh: 時薛懷義、張易之、昌宗皆承恩顧。

translations.literal: At the time Xue Huaiyi, Zhang Yizhi, and Changzong all received imperial favor and attention.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Xue Huaiyi, Zhang Yizhi, and Zhang Changzong all enjoyed the empress's intimate favor.

sentences.zh: 三思與承嗣每折節事之。

translations.literal: Sansi and Chengsi each humiliated themselves to serve them.
translations.idiomatic: Sansi and Chengsi abased themselves to wait on these favorites.

sentences.zh: 懷義欲乘馬，承嗣、三思必為之執轡。

translations.literal: When Huaiyi wished to mount a horse, Chengsi and Sansi would invariably hold the reins for him.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Huaiyi wanted to ride, Chengsi and Sansi would hold his stirrups.

sentences.zh: 又贈昌宗詩，盛稱昌宗才貌是王子晉後身，仍令朝士遞相屬和。

translations.literal: He also presented Changzong with a poem, lavishly praising Changzong's talent and appearance as the reincarnation of Prince Zijing, and had court officials compose matching verses in turn.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote Changzong a poem comparing his talent and looks to the reincarnation of Prince Zijing, and had court officials compose matching verses in succession.

sentences.zh: 三思又以則天厭居深宮，又欲與張易之、昌宗等扈從馳騁，以弄其權。

translations.literal: Sansi also knew that Zetian wearied of dwelling deep in the palace, and wished to accompany Zhang Yizhi, Changzong, and the rest in riding and hunting, thereby wielding his influence.
translations.idiomatic: Sansi also knew Zetian chafed at palace confinement and wanted to ride and hunt alongside Zhang Yizhi, Changzong, and the others so he could exercise power at her side.

sentences.zh: 乃請創造三陽宮於嵩高山，興泰宮於萬壽山，請則天每歲臨幸，前後工役甚眾，百姓怨之。

translations.literal: He therefore requested the creation of the Sanyang Palace on Mount Songgao and the Xingtai Palace on Mount Wanshou, asking that Zetian visit each year — the laborers conscripted before and after were very numerous, and the people resented it.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore proposed building the Sanyang Palace on Mount Song and the Xingtai Palace on Mount Wanshou, urging Zetian to visit each year; the massive conscription of labor before and after provoked widespread public resentment.

sentences.zh: 神龍初，進拜司空、同中書門下三品，加實封五百戶，固辭不受。

translations.literal: Early in Shenlong, he was promoted to Minister of Works and Co-Minister of the Secretariat and Chancellery of the Third Rank, with an additional taxable fief of five hundred households; he firmly declined and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Shenlong era he was promoted to minister of works and co-minister of the secretariat and chancellery of the third rank, with an additional five hundred taxable households, but firmly refused the appointment.

sentences.zh: 未幾，隨例降封為德靜郡王，量減實封二百戶。

translations.literal: Before long, following precedent his rank was reduced to Prince of Dejing Commandery, with his taxable fief measuredly reduced by two hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, following the general demotion of the Wu clan, he was reduced to Prince of Dejing Commandery and lost two hundred taxable households.

sentences.zh: 尋拜左散騎常侍，則天遺制令復其所減實封。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Left Regular Attendant of the Cavalry; Zetian's death decree ordered restoration of the reduced taxable fief.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed left regular attendant of the cavalry; Zetian's dying edict restored the taxable households that had been taken away.

sentences.zh: 初，敬暉等立功後，掌知國政，三思慮其更為己患，而令其子崇訓因安樂公主構誣敬暉等，並流於嶺表而死。

translations.literal: Initially, after Jing Hui and the others had achieved merit and controlled state affairs, Sansi feared they would again become a threat to him; he had his son Chongxun, through Princess Anle, fabricate charges against Jing Hui and the others, and they were all exiled to the region beyond the mountains and died there.
translations.idiomatic: After Jing Hui and his allies seized power for restoring the Tang, Sansi feared they would turn on him; through Princess Anle his son Chongxun fabricated charges against them, and they were all exiled beyond the mountains to their deaths.

sentences.zh: 自是三思威權日盛，軍國政事，多所參綜。

translations.literal: From this time Sansi's power and authority grew daily; he participated widely in military and state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: From then on Sansi's power swelled daily, and he meddled in both military and civil governance.

sentences.zh: 敬暉等所斥黜者，皆能引復舊職，令百官復修則天之法。

translations.literal: Those whom Jing Hui and the others had dismissed he was able to restore to their former posts; he ordered the hundred officials to again practice Zetian's laws.
translations.idiomatic: He restored to office everyone Jing Hui had removed and ordered the bureaucracy to revert to Zetian's policies.

sentences.zh: 時人皆言其陰懷篡逆，以比曹孟德、司馬仲達。

translations.literal: People of the time all said he secretly harbored usurpation, comparing him to Cao Mengde and Sima Zhongda.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries whispered that he secretly plotted usurpation, comparing him to Cao Cao and Sima Yi.

sentences.zh: 雍州人韋月將、高軫等並上疏言三思父子必為逆亂。

translations.literal: Wei Yuejiang of Yong Prefecture, Gao Zhen, and others all submitted memorials saying that Sansi and his son would surely rebel.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Yuejiang of Yong Prefecture, Gao Zhen, and others submitted memorials warning that Sansi and his son were bound to rebel.

sentences.zh: 三思知而求索其罪。

translations.literal: Sansi learned of it and sought their crimes.
translations.idiomatic: When Sansi learned of this, he set out to find grounds to prosecute them.

sentences.zh: 有司希旨，奏：「月將坐當棄市，軫配流嶺外」。

translations.literal: The relevant offices, eager to please, reported: "Yuejiang's offense warrants death by public execution; Zhen is sentenced to exile beyond the mountains."
translations.idiomatic: The judicial offices, eager to please him, recommended: "Yuejiang deserves execution by quartering; Zhen should be exiled beyond the mountains."

sentences.zh: 黃門侍郎宋璟執奏云：「月將所犯，不合至死。」

translations.literal: Vice Director of the Yellow Gate Song Jing firmly submitted, saying: "The offense Yuejiang committed does not warrant death."
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director Song Jing of the Yellow Gate protested: "Yuejiang's offense does not merit death."

sentences.zh: 三思怒，竟斥宋璟為外職。

translations.literal: Sansi was angry and ultimately expelled Song Jing to an outside post.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, Sansi had Song Jing banished to a provincial post.

sentences.zh: 三思既猜嫉正士，嘗言「不知何等名作好人，唯有向我好者，是好人耳。」

translations.literal: Sansi, already suspicious and jealous of upright men, once said, "I know not what is called being a good person — only those who are good to me are good people."
translations.idiomatic: Sansi, already paranoid toward upright officials, once declared, "I don't know what makes a good man—only those who are good to me count as good."

sentences.zh: 又與其所親兵部尚書宗楚客、將作大匠宗晉卿、太府卿紀處訥、鴻臚卿甘元柬遞相引致，幹黷時政。

translations.literal: He also mutually promoted with his intimates — Minister of War Zong Chuke, Commissioner of Imperial Construction Zong Jinqing, Minister of the Court of the Treasury Ji Chune, and Minister of Diplomatic Reception Gan Yuanjian — interfering impertinently in the affairs of the time.
translations.idiomatic: He also colluded with his cronies—Minister of War Zong Chuke, Commissioner of Imperial Construction Zong Jinqing, Minister of the Treasury Ji Chune, and Minister of Diplomatic Reception Gan Yuanjian—recklessly meddling in state affairs.

sentences.zh: 侍御史周利用、冉祖雍，太僕丞李悛，光祿丞宋之遜，監察御史姚紹之等五人，常為其耳目，時人呼為「三思五狗」。

translations.literal: Supervising Censor Zhou Liyong, Ran Zuyong, Assistant Commissioner of the Imperial Stud Li Quan, Assistant Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments Song Zhixun, and Investigating Censor Yao Shaozhi — these five men constantly served as his eyes and ears; people of the time called them "Sansi's Five Dogs."
translations.idiomatic: Supervising censor Zhou Liyong, Ran Zuyong, assistant commissioner of the imperial stud Li Quan, assistant director of the court of imperial entertainments Song Zhixun, and investigating censor Yao Shaozhi—these five served as his spies, and people called them "Sansi's Five Dogs."

sentences.zh: 中宗尋又制：武氏崇恩廟，一依天授時舊禮享祭，其吳陵、順陵，並置官員，皆三思意也。

translations.literal: Zhongzong soon also decreed: the Wu clan's Chong'en Temple was to be served with sacrificial rites according entirely to the old ritual of the Tianshou era; Wu Ling and Shun Ling were each provided officials — all at Sansi's instigation.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzong soon decreed that the Wu clan's Chong'en Temple be maintained under the sacrificial rites of the Tianshou era, and that officials be appointed for the Wu and Shun tombs—all at Sansi's urging.

sentences.zh: 三思既與韋庶人及上官昭容私通，嘗忌節湣太子，又因安樂公主密謀廢黜之。

translations.literal: Sansi, having already had illicit relations with Empress Wei the commoner and Shangguan Zhaorong, had long resented Crown Prince Jiemin; through Princess Anle he also secretly plotted to depose him.
translations.idiomatic: Sansi, who was already secretly involved with Empress Wei and Shangguan Zhaorong, had long resented Crown Prince Jiemin and conspired with Princess Anle to have him deposed.

sentences.zh: 三年七月，太子率羽林大將軍李多祚等，發左右羽林兵，殺三思及其子崇訓於其第，並殺其親黨十餘人。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the third year, the crown prince led General of the Feathered Forest Li Duozuo and others, mobilizing the Left and Right Feathered Forest armies, and killed Sansi and his son Chongxun at his residence, also killing more than ten of his close partisans.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the third year, the crown prince led General of the Feathered Forest Li Duozuo and others in mobilizing the Left and Right Feathered Forest armies, killing Sansi and his son Chongxun at Sansi's residence along with more than ten of their close associates.

sentences.zh: 俄而事變，太子既死，中宗為三思舉哀，廢朝五日，贈太尉，追封梁王，謚曰宣。

translations.literal: Soon the affair changed; once the crown prince was dead, Zhongzong held mourning for Sansi, suspended court for five days, posthumously granted him Grand Commandant, posthumously enfeoffed him as King of Liang, with posthumous title Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: When the coup reversed itself and the crown prince was killed, Zhongzong mourned Sansi, suspended court for five days, posthumously made him grand commandant and Prince of Liang, and gave him the posthumous title Xuan.

sentences.zh: 安樂公主又以節湣太子首致祭於三思及崇訓靈柩前。

translations.literal: Princess Anle also had Crown Prince Jiemin's head brought to offer sacrifice before the bier of Sansi and Chongxun.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Anle even had Crown Prince Jiemin's severed head brought to Sansi and Chongxun's coffins as an offering.

sentences.zh: 睿宗踐祚，以三思父子俱有逆節，制令斫棺暴屍，平其墳墓。

translations.literal: When Ruizong ascended the throne, because Sansi and his son both had treacherous conduct, he decreed that their coffins be opened and corpses exposed, and their tombs leveled.
translations.idiomatic: When Ruizong took the throne, he ordered Sansi and his son's coffins opened, their corpses exposed, and their tombs demolished for their treason.

sentences.zh: 三思子　崇訓崇訓，三思第二子也。

translations.literal: Sansi's son Chongxun. Chongxun was Sansi's second son.
translations.idiomatic: Sansi's son Chongxun. Chongxun was Sansi's second son.

sentences.zh: 則天時，封為高陽郡王。

translations.literal: In Zetian's time, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Gaoyang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zetian he was enfeoffed as Prince of Gaoyang Commandery.

sentences.zh: 長安中，尚安樂郡主。

translations.literal: During the Chang'an era, he married the Princess of Anle Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chang'an era he married the Princess of Anle Commandery.

sentences.zh: 時三思用事於朝，欲寵其禮。

translations.literal: At the time Sansi wielded power at court and wished to lavish honor on the wedding rites.
translations.idiomatic: Sansi then dominated the court and wanted the wedding celebrated with extraordinary pomp.

sentences.zh: 中宗為太子在東宮，三思宅在天津橋南，自重光門內行親迎禮，歸於其宅。

translations.literal: Zhongzong was crown prince in the Eastern Palace; Sansi's residence was south of the Tianjin Bridge; the bridegroom's reception ceremony was conducted from within the Chongguang Gate and returned to his residence.
translations.idiomatic: With Zhongzong still crown prince in the Eastern Palace, Sansi's mansion stood south of the Tianjin Bridge; the formal bride-fetching procession set out from within the Chongguang Gate and returned to Sansi's home.

sentences.zh: 三思又令宰臣李嶠、蘇味道，詞人沈佺期、宋之問、徐彥伯、張說、閻朝隱、崔融、崔湜、鄭愔等賦《花燭行》以美之。

translations.literal: Sansi also had chancellors Li Qiao and Su Weidao, and poets Shen Quanqi, Song Zhiwen, Xu Yanbo, Zhang Yue, Yan Chaoyin, Cui Rong, Cui Shi, and Zheng Yin compose "Song of the Flower Candle" to praise the occasion.
translations.idiomatic: Sansi also commissioned chancellors Li Qiao and Su Weidao and poets Shen Quanqi, Song Zhiwen, Xu Yanbo, Zhang Yue, Yan Chaoyin, Cui Rong, Cui Shi, and Zheng Yin to compose "Song of the Flower Candle" in celebration.

sentences.zh: 其時張易之、昌宗、宗楚客兄弟貴盛，時假詞於人，皆有新句。

translations.literal: At that time Zhang Yizhi, Changzong, and the Zong Chuke brothers were mighty in rank and splendor; they often borrowed others' words and all had fresh lines.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yizhi, Changzong, and the Zong Chuke brothers were then at the height of power and often had ghostwriters supply them with polished new lines.

sentences.zh: 崇訓授左衛中郎將。

translations.literal: Chongxun was appointed Captain in the Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Chongxun was appointed captain in the Left Guard.

sentences.zh: 神龍元年，拜駙馬都尉，遷太常卿，兼左衛將軍。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shenlong, he was appointed Commandant of Horsemen for the Imperial Son-in-Law, transferred to Minister of Ceremonies, and concurrently General of the Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Shenlong he was made imperial son-in-law commandant, then minister of ceremonies and concurrently general of the Left Guard.

sentences.zh: 降封酆國公，仍賜實封五百戶，尋徙封鎬國公。

translations.literal: His rank was reduced to Duke of Feng State, yet he was granted a taxable fief of five hundred households; soon he was transferred to Duke of Hao State.
translations.idiomatic: He was demoted to Duke of Feng but kept a taxable fief of five hundred households; soon his title was changed to Duke of Hao.

sentences.zh: 二年，兼太子賓客，攝左衛將軍。

translations.literal: In the second year, he was concurrently Mentor to the Heir Apparent and acting General of the Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was made mentor to the heir apparent and acting general of the Left Guard.

sentences.zh: 及為節湣太子所殺，優制贈開府儀同三司，追贈魯王，謚曰忠。

translations.literal: When he was killed by Crown Prince Jiemin, an exceptional decree posthumously granted him Forte of the First Rank with Protocol Equal to the Three Ducal Ministers, posthumously enfeoffed him as King of Lu, with posthumous title Zhong.
translations.idiomatic: After Crown Prince Jiemin killed him, an extraordinary edict posthumously granted him the rank of grand preceptor with the protocol of the three ducal ministers, made him Prince of Lu, and gave him the posthumous name Loyal.

sentences.zh: 從祖弟　懿宗懿宗，則天伯父士逸之孫也。

translations.literal: Paternal cousin Yizong. Yizong was the grandson of Zetian's paternal uncle Shiyi.
translations.idiomatic: Paternal cousin Yizong. Yizong was the grandson of Zetian's paternal uncle Shiyi.

sentences.zh: 父元忠，高宗時仕至倉部郎中。

translations.literal: His father Yuanzhong, during Gaozong's reign, rose to Bureau Director of Granaries in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yuanzhong rose during Gaozong's reign to bureau director of granaries in the ministry of revenue.

sentences.zh: 天授年，封士逸為蜀王，懿宗封為河內郡王，歷遷洛州長史、左金吾衛大將軍。

translations.literal: In the Tianshou era, Shiyi was enfeoffed as King of Shu; Yizong was enfeoffed as Prince of Henan Commandery; he successively served as Chief Administrator of Luo Prefecture and General of the Left Golden Crow Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tianshou era Shiyi was enfeoffed as Prince of Shu and Yizong as Prince of Henan Commandery; Yizong later served as chief administrator of Luo Prefecture and general of the Left Golden Crow Guard.

sentences.zh: 萬歲通天年中，契丹賊帥孫萬榮寇河北，命懿宗為大總管討之。

translations.literal: In the Wansui Tongtian era, the Khitan bandit chief Sun Wanrong invaded Hebei; Yizong was appointed Great Commander-in-Chief to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: During the Wansui Tongtian era, when the Khitan chieftain Sun Wanrong raided Hebei, Yizong was appointed supreme commander to suppress him.

sentences.zh: 軍次趙州，用聞賊將至冀州，懿宗懼，便欲棄軍而遁。

translations.literal: The army halted at Zhao Prefecture; upon hearing the bandits were about to reach Ji Prefecture, Yizong was afraid and wished to abandon the army and flee.
translations.idiomatic: His army halted at Zhao Prefecture; when he heard the rebels were heading for Ji Prefecture, Yizong panicked and wanted to abandon his troops and flee.

sentences.zh: 人或謂曰：「賊眾極多，然其軍無輜重，以抄掠為資，若按兵以守，勢必離散，因而擊之。

translations.literal: Someone said to him: "The bandits are extremely numerous, yet their army has no baggage train and subsists on plunder; if you hold your troops and stand on the defensive, they will inevitably scatter — strike them then.
translations.idiomatic: Someone advised him: "The enemy is vast, but they carry no supplies and live by looting; if you hold your ground, they will scatter—then strike.

sentences.zh: 可有大功也。」

translations.literal: You can achieve great merit."
translations.idiomatic: You can win a great victory."

sentences.zh: 懿宗不聽，遂退據相州，時人嗤其怯懦。

translations.literal: Yizong would not listen; he withdrew and took up position at Xiang Prefecture; people of the time mocked his cowardice.
translations.idiomatic: Yizong refused to listen, retreated to Xiang Prefecture, and was widely ridiculed for his cowardice.

sentences.zh: 由是賊眾進屠趙州而去。

translations.literal: Thereupon the bandit force advanced, slaughtered Zhao Prefecture, and departed.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels then marched on, massacred Zhao Prefecture, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 尋又令懿宗安撫河北諸州。

translations.literal: Soon Yizong was again ordered to pacify the various prefectures of Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: Yizong was soon ordered to pacify the prefectures of Hebei.

sentences.zh: 先是，百姓有脅從賊眾，後得歸來者。

translations.literal: Previously, there were commoners who had been coerced into following the bandit host and later managed to return.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, many locals had been forced to join the rebels and later made their way home.

sentences.zh: 懿宗以為同反，總殺之。

translations.literal: Yizong regarded them as fellow rebels and killed them all.
translations.idiomatic: Yizong treated them all as collaborators and had them executed.

sentences.zh: 仍生刳取其膽，後行刑，流血盈前，言笑自若。

translations.literal: He still extracted their gall while they were alive; afterward as executions proceeded, blood filled the ground before him, yet he spoke and laughed as if at ease.
translations.idiomatic: He even had their gall cut out while they were still alive; as the killing continued and blood pooled at his feet, he chatted and laughed as if unmoved.

sentences.zh: 初。

translations.literal: At first.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier still,

sentences.zh: 孫萬榮別帥何阿小攻陷冀州，亦多屠害士女。

translations.literal: Sun Wanrong's lieutenant He Axiao had attacked and taken Ji Prefecture, also slaughtering many men and women.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Wanrong's lieutenant He Axiao had captured Ji Prefecture and slaughtered countless civilians.

sentences.zh: 至是，時人號懿宗與阿小為兩何，為之語曰：「唯此兩何，殺人最多。」

translations.literal: By this time, people of the time nicknamed Yizong and Axiao "the two Hes," making a saying: "Of these two Hes alone, the most people were killed."
translations.idiomatic: By then people nicknamed Yizong and Axiao "the two Hes," coining the saying: "These two Hes alone have killed the most."

sentences.zh: 懿宗又自天授已來，嘗受中旨，推鞫制獄，王公大臣，多被陷成其罪，時人以為周興、來俊臣之亞焉。

translations.literal: From Tianshou onward, Yizong had also frequently received secret imperial orders, conducting interrogations in specially designated prisons; kings, dukes, and high ministers were often framed and convicted on his account; people of the time regarded him as second only to Zhou Xing and Lai Junchen.
translations.idiomatic: From the Tianshou era on, Yizong had also carried out secret interrogations by imperial order; princes and ministers alike were often framed on his word, and contemporaries ranked him just below Zhou Xing and Lai Junchen among the dynasty's torturers.

sentences.zh: 神龍初，隨例降爵，封耿國公，累轉懷州刺史，尋卒。

translations.literal: Early in Shenlong, following precedent his noble rank was reduced; he was enfeoffed as Duke of Geng State, successively transferred to Prefect of Huai Prefecture, and soon died.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Shenlong era he was demoted under the general reduction of Wu titles to Duke of Geng, later served as prefect of Huai Prefecture, and soon died.

sentences.zh: 從父弟　攸暨攸暨，則天伯父士讓孫也。

translations.literal: Paternal cousin Youji. Youji was the grandson of Zetian's paternal uncle Shirang.
translations.idiomatic: Paternal cousin Youji. Youji was the grandson of Zetian's paternal uncle Shirang.

sentences.zh: 天授中，封士讓為楚王，攸暨封千乘郡王。

translations.literal: During Tianshou, Shirang was enfeoffed as King of Chu; Youji was enfeoffed as Prince of Qiansheng Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianshou era Shirang was enfeoffed as Prince of Chu and Youji as Prince of Qiansheng Commandery.

sentences.zh: 賜爵實封三百戶。

translations.literal: He was granted a noble title with a taxable fief of three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: He received a noble title with a taxable fief of three hundred households.

sentences.zh: 兄攸寧為建昌郡王，實封四百戶。

translations.literal: His elder brother Youning was Prince of Jianchang Commandery with a taxable fief of four hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Youning was Prince of Jianchang Commandery with four hundred taxable households.

sentences.zh: 攸寧歷遷鳳閣侍郎、納言、冬官尚書，病卒。

translations.literal: Youning successively served as Vice Director of the Phoenix Pavilion, Censor-in-Chief, and Minister of Works; he died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Youning served successively as vice director of the Phoenix Pavilion, censor-in-chief, and minister of works before dying of illness.

sentences.zh: 攸暨初為右衛中郎將，尚太平公主，授駙馬都尉。

translations.literal: Youji initially served as Captain in the Right Guard; he married Princess Taiping and was appointed Commandant of Horsemen for the Imperial Son-in-Law.
translations.idiomatic: Youji began as captain in the Right Guard; he married Princess Taiping and was appointed imperial son-in-law commandant.

sentences.zh: 累遷右衛將軍，進封定王，又加實封三百戶。

translations.literal: He was successively promoted to General of the Right Guard, advanced to Prince of Ding, and granted an additional taxable fief of three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to general of the Right Guard, was advanced to Prince of Ding, and received an additional three hundred taxable households.

sentences.zh: 俄又改安定郡王，歷遷司禮卿、左散騎常侍，加特進。

translations.literal: Soon he was changed to Prince of Anding Commandery; he successively served as Minister of Rites and Left Regular Attendant of the Cavalry, and was granted Special Advancement.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Prince of Anding Commandery, served as minister of rites and left regular attendant of the cavalry, and was granted special advancement.

sentences.zh: 神龍中，拜司徒，復封定王，實封滿一千戶，固辭不拜。

translations.literal: During Shenlong, he was appointed Minister of Education, again enfeoffed as Prince of Ding with a taxable fief reaching one thousand households; he firmly declined and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shenlong era he was offered the post of minister of education and restoration as Prince of Ding with a full thousand taxable households, but firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 尋而隨例降封樂壽郡王，拜右散騎常侍，加開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: Soon, following precedent, he was reduced to Prince of Leshou Commandery, appointed Right Regular Attendant of the Cavalry, and granted Forte of the First Rank with Protocol Equal to the Three Ducal Ministers.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon demoted under precedent to Prince of Leshou Commandery, appointed right regular attendant of the cavalry, and granted the rank of grand preceptor with the protocol of the three ducal ministers.

sentences.zh: 延秀等誅後，又降封楚國公。

translations.literal: After Yanxiu and the others were executed, he was again reduced to Duke of Chu State.
translations.idiomatic: After Yanxiu and the others were executed, he was demoted again to Duke of Chu.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈太尉、并州大都督，追封定王。

translations.literal: He died; he was posthumously granted Grand Commandant and Grand Governor of Bingzhou, and posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Ding.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, he was posthumously made grand commandant and grand governor of Bingzhou and enfeoffed as Prince of Ding.

sentences.zh: 尋以公主謀逆，令平毀其墓。

translations.literal: Soon, because the princess plotted rebellion, he was ordered to have his tomb leveled and destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after the princess's treason plot, the court ordered his tomb demolished.

sentences.zh: 太平公主者，高宗少女也。

translations.literal: Princess Taiping was the youngest daughter of Emperor Gaozong.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Taiping was Emperor Gaozong's youngest daughter.

sentences.zh: 以則天所生，特承恩寵。

translations.literal: Because she was born of Zetian, she received special grace and favor.
translations.idiomatic: As Zetian's own daughter, she enjoyed extraordinary favor.

sentences.zh: 初，永隆年降駙馬薛紹。

translations.literal: At first, in the Yonglong era she was married to Imperial Son-in-Law Xue Shao.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yonglong era she was first married to the imperial son-in-law Xue Shao.

sentences.zh: 紹，垂拱中被誣告與諸王連謀伏誅，則天私殺攸暨之妻以配主焉。

translations.literal: Shao, in the Chuigong era, was falsely accused of conspiring with the princes and was executed; Zetian secretly killed Youji's wife to give her to the princess in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chuigong era Shao was falsely accused of plotting with the princes and executed; Zetian secretly had Youji's wife killed so the princess could marry Youji.

sentences.zh: 公主豐碩，方額廣頤，多權略，則天以為類己，每預謀議，宮禁嚴峻，事不令泄。

translations.literal: The princess was plump and robust, with a square forehead and broad cheeks; she was full of stratagems. Zetian thought her like herself, and each time included her in deliberations; the palace prohibitions were severe, and matters were not permitted to leak out.
translations.idiomatic: Full-bodied, with a broad forehead and cheeks, she was clever in intrigue. Zetian saw in her a kindred spirit and brought her into every counsel; palace security was strict and nothing was allowed to leak out.

sentences.zh: 公主亦畏懼自檢，但崇飾邸第。

translations.literal: The princess also feared and restrained herself, only adorning her mansion lavishly.
translations.idiomatic: The princess too was cautious and self-restrained, limiting herself to sumptuous embellishment of her residence.

sentences.zh: 二十餘年，天下獨有太平一公主，父為帝，母為后，夫為親王，子為郡王，貴盛無比。

translations.literal: For more than twenty years, in all the realm there was only Princess Taiping alone: her father was emperor, her mother empress, her husband an imperial prince, her sons princes of commanderies — splendor and eminence without equal.
translations.idiomatic: For more than twenty years no one in the empire matched Princess Taiping: emperor for a father, empress for a mother, an imperial prince for a husband, commandery princes for sons — her glory was unmatched.

sentences.zh: 永淳已前朝制，親王食實封八百戶，有至一千戶；

translations.literal: Under court regulations before Yongchun, imperial princes enjoyed taxable fiefs of eight hundred households, some reaching one thousand households;
translations.idiomatic: Before the Yongchun era, imperial princes normally received taxable fiefs of eight hundred households, some as many as a thousand;

sentences.zh: 公主出降三百戶，公主加五十戶。

translations.literal: princesses upon marriage three hundred households, with an additional fifty for princesses.
translations.idiomatic: princesses received three hundred households upon marriage, plus an additional fifty.

sentences.zh: 太平食湯沐之邑一千二百戶，聖歷初加至三千戶，

translations.literal: Taiping received a bath-and-fief domain of twelve hundred households; at the beginning of Shenglì it was increased to three thousand households,
translations.idiomatic: Taiping held a fief of twelve hundred households for her support; at the start of the Shenglì era this rose to three thousand.

sentences.zh: 預誅張易之謀有功，進號鎮國太平公主，相王加號安國相王，並食實封通前五千戶，賞賜不可勝紀。

translations.literal: for meritorious service in the plot to execute Zhang Yizhi, she was advanced to the title Pacifying-the-Realm Princess Taiping; the Prince of Xiang was additionally titled Pacifying-the-Realm Prince of Xiang; both received taxable fiefs reaching five thousand households in all with previous grants; rewards and gifts were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: For her role in the plot against Zhang Yizhi, she was given the title Pacifying-the-Realm Princess Taiping and the Prince of Xiang became Pacifying-the-Realm Prince of Xiang; their combined taxable fiefs reached five thousand households, with rewards beyond reckoning.

sentences.zh: 公主孽氏二男二女，武氏二男一女，並食實封。

translations.literal: The princess's children by concubines — two sons and two daughters; Wu clan children — two sons and one daughter — all received taxable fiefs.
translations.idiomatic: Her children by concubines—two sons and two daughters—and her Wu-clan children—two sons and one daughter—all received taxable fiefs.

sentences.zh: 又相王、衛王重俊、成王千里宅，遣衛士宿衛，環其所居，十步置一仗舍，持兵巡僥，同於宮禁。

translations.literal: Also at the residences of the Prince of Xiang, Prince of Wei Chongjun, and Prince of Cheng Qianli, guards were dispatched for overnight protection, encircling where they dwelt; every ten paces an arms-shed was placed; men bearing weapons patrolled watchfully — the same as within the palace prohibitions.
translations.idiomatic: Guard detachments were posted around the mansions of the Prince of Xiang, Prince of Wei Chongjun, and Prince of Cheng Qianli; an armory was set up every ten paces, armed patrols circled their compounds — security rivaling the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 太平、長寧、安樂三公主，置鋪一如親王。

translations.literal: The three princesses Taiping, Changning, and Anle had commercial establishments set up just like imperial princes.
translations.idiomatic: Princesses Taiping, Changning, and Anle were granted commercial establishments equal to those of imperial princes.

sentences.zh: 二年正月，置公主府，

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year, princess households were established,
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the second year of Jinglong, official princess households were established.

sentences.zh: 公主男崇簡、崇敏、崇行，同授三品，與漁陽王兄弟四人同制。

translations.literal: the princess's sons Chongjian, Chongmin, and Chongxing were all granted third rank together, on the same terms as the four brothers of the Prince of Yuyang.
translations.idiomatic: Her sons Chongjian, Chongmin, and Chongxing were all appointed to third rank, on the same terms granted the Prince of Yuyang's four brothers.

sentences.zh: 時中宗仁善，韋后、上官昭容用事禁中，皆以為智謀不及公主，甚憚之。

translations.literal: At the time Zhongzong was benevolent and mild; Empress Wei and Shangguan Zhaorong wielded power within the palace — both considered their wisdom and schemes inferior to the princess's, and greatly feared her.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzong was mild by nature; Empress Wei and Shangguan Zhaorong ran affairs inside the palace, but both knew themselves outmatched by the princess in wit and strategy and feared her deeply.

sentences.zh: 公主日益豪橫，進達朝士，多至大官，詞人後進造其門者，或有貧窘，則遺之金帛，士亦翕然稱之。

translations.literal: The princess daily grew more domineering and overbearing; she promoted court gentlemen, many reaching high office; literati and rising scholars who came to her gate — some in poverty and want — she would bestow gold and silk upon; gentlemen also uniformly praised her.
translations.idiomatic: She grew daily more arrogant, advancing courtiers—many to high office. Young poets and scholars who visited her door in poverty received gold and silk, and the literati praised her lavishly.

sentences.zh: 及六月，韋后作逆稱制，偽尊溫王。

translations.literal: When the sixth month came, Empress Wei committed treason and assumed imperial authority, falsely elevating Prince Wen.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Empress Wei usurped power and installed Prince Wen as a puppet ruler.

sentences.zh: 玄宗居臨淄邸，憤之，將清內難。

translations.literal: Xuanzong dwelt at the Linzi residence; enraged, he prepared to quell the internal crisis.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong, living at the Linzi residence, was furious and prepared to put down the coup.

sentences.zh: 公主又預其謀，令男崇簡從之。

translations.literal: The princess again participated in his plot, ordering her son Chongjian to follow him.
translations.idiomatic: The princess joined the plot and sent her son Chongjian to support him.

sentences.zh: 及立溫王，數日，天下之心歸於相府，難為其議。

translations.literal: Once Prince Wen was established, within days the hearts of the realm turned to the Xiang residence; it was difficult to proceed with that plan.
translations.idiomatic: Within days of Prince Wen's enthronement, public sentiment shifted to the Prince of Xiang, making the original plan untenable.

sentences.zh: 公主入啟幼主，以王室多故，資於長君，乃提下幼主，因與玄宗、大臣尊立睿宗。

translations.literal: The princess entered and addressed the young sovereign, saying that with many troubles in the royal house, reliance should be placed on the elder ruler; she then brought down the young sovereign, and together with Xuanzong and the ministers honored and established Ruizong.
translations.idiomatic: The princess persuaded the child emperor that the throne needed an experienced ruler; she had him step down, and with Xuanzong and the ministers enthroned Ruizong.

sentences.zh: 公主頻著大勛，益尊重，乃加實封五千戶，通前滿一萬戶。

translations.literal: The princess repeatedly achieved great merit and grew ever more honored; she was then granted an additional taxable fief of five thousand households, reaching ten thousand households in all with previous grants.
translations.idiomatic: For her repeated great service she was held in still higher esteem and granted five thousand additional taxable households, bringing her total to ten thousand.

sentences.zh: 公主子崇行、崇敏、崇簡三人，封異姓王；

translations.literal: The princess's sons Chongxing, Chongmin, and Chongjian — three men — were enfeoffed as kings of a different surname;
translations.idiomatic: Her sons Chongxing, Chongmin, and Chongjian were enfeoffed as princes bearing non-imperial surnames;

sentences.zh: 崇行國子祭酒，四人九卿三品。

translations.literal: Chongxing was made Chancellor of the Directorate of Education; four men held posts among the nine ministers at third rank.
translations.idiomatic: Chongxing became chancellor of the Directorate of Education; four family members held third-rank posts among the nine ministries.

sentences.zh: 每入奏事，坐語移時，所言皆聽。

translations.literal: Each time she entered to report on affairs, she would sit and speak for a long while; whatever she said was heeded.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever she came to audience she would sit and talk at length, and the emperor accepted all she proposed.

sentences.zh: 薦人或驟歷清職，或至南北衙將相，權移人主。

translations.literal: Those she recommended might suddenly pass through pure offices, or reach minister and general posts in the southern and northern bureaus; power shifted from the sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: Her protégés leapt into prestigious posts or rose to chancellor and general in the central and military administrations; real power shifted from the throne.

sentences.zh: 軍國大政，事必參決，如不朝謁，則宰臣就第議其可否。

translations.literal: On great affairs of army and state she necessarily joined in deciding; if she did not attend court, chancellors would go to her residence to discuss what was feasible or not.
translations.idiomatic: On all major civil and military matters she had a decisive voice; when she skipped court, chancellors came to her mansion to consult her.

sentences.zh: 公主由是滋驕，田園遍於近甸膏腴，而市易造作器物，吳、蜀、嶺南供送，相屬於路。

translations.literal: The princess thereby grew ever prouder; fields and gardens spread throughout the fertile lands of the near suburbs; trade and manufacture of goods — Wu, Shu, and Lingnan all sent tribute — followed one another on the roads.
translations.idiomatic: She grew ever more arrogant. Her estates covered the fertile suburbs near the capital; goods from Wu, Shu, and Lingnan streamed along the roads to supply her trade and workshops.

sentences.zh: 綺疏寶帳，音樂輿乘，同於宮掖。

translations.literal: Ornate lattices and jeweled canopies, music and carriages — the same as in the palace women's quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Her carved screens, jeweled hangings, musicians, and carriages rivaled the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 侍兒披羅綺，常數百人，蒼頭監嫗，必盈千數。

translations.literal: Serving girls robed in gauze and silk often numbered in the hundreds; male servants and overseer women necessarily exceeded a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Hundreds of maids in silks waited on her; male servants and stewardesses numbered over a thousand.

sentences.zh: 外州供狗馬玩好滋味，不可紀極。

translations.literal: Outer prefectures supplied dogs, horses, curios, and delicacies — beyond all reckoning.
translations.idiomatic: Outlying prefectures sent hounds, horses, luxuries, and delicacies beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 有胡僧惠範，家富於財寶，善事權貴，公主與之私，奏為聖善寺主，加三品，封公，殖貨流於江劍。

translations.literal: There was the foreign monk Huifan, whose household was rich in treasure; skilled at serving the powerful and noble — the princess had a private affair with him; she memorialized to make him abbot of Shengshan Temple, grant third rank, enfeoff him as duke; profit-seeking flowed along the Yangzi and Jian regions.
translations.idiomatic: A foreign monk named Huifan, enormously wealthy and adept at currying favor with the powerful, became her lover. She had him appointed abbot of Shengshan Temple, raised to third rank, and enfeoffed as duke; his commercial ventures spread through the Yangzi and Sichuan region.

sentences.zh: 公主懼玄宗英武，乃連結將相，專謀異計。

translations.literal: The princess feared Xuanzong's martial prowess; she then linked up with generals and chancellors, exclusively plotting separatist designs.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing Xuanzong's martial prowess, she built a faction among generals and chancellors and plotted treason.

sentences.zh: 其時宰相七人，五出公主門，常元楷、李慈掌禁兵，常私謁公主。

translations.literal: At that time among seven chancellors, five had come from the princess's gate; Chang Yuankai and Li Ci controlled the forbidden armies and often paid private visits to the princess.
translations.idiomatic: Of the seven chancellors then in office, five were her clients; Chang Yuankai and Li Ci, who controlled the palace guard, visited her privately.

sentences.zh: 七月，玄宗在武德殿，事漸危逼，乃勒兵誅其黨竇懷貞、蕭至忠、岑羲等，公主遽入山寺，數日方出，賜死於家。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, Xuanzong was at Wude Hall; as matters grew increasingly perilous, he mobilized troops and executed her partisans Dou Huaiyi, Xiao Zhizhong, Cen Xi, and others; the princess suddenly entered a mountain temple; several days passed before she came out; she was ordered to die at home.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month, as the crisis mounted at Wude Hall, Xuanzong mobilized troops and executed her allies Dou Huaiyi, Xiao Zhizhong, and Cen Xi. The princess fled to a mountain monastery; days later she emerged and was ordered to take her own life at home.

sentences.zh: 公主諸子及黨與死者數十人。

translations.literal: The princess's sons and party associates who died numbered several tens.
translations.idiomatic: Dozens of her sons and followers were killed.

sentences.zh: 籍其家，財貨山積，珍奇寶物，侔於御府，馬牧羊牧田園質庫，數年徵斂不盡。

translations.literal: Her household was inventoried; goods and wealth piled like mountains; rare and marvelous treasures equaled the imperial treasury; horses, sheep, pastures, fields, gardens, and pawnshops — levies for years could not exhaust them.
translations.idiomatic: When her estate was confiscated, wealth piled like mountains and treasures rivaled the imperial storehouse; horses, flocks, farms, gardens, and pawnshops yielded levies for years without being exhausted.

sentences.zh: 惠範家產亦數十萬貫。

translations.literal: Huifan's household assets also amounted to several hundred thousand strings of cash.
translations.idiomatic: Huifan's estate too was worth several hundred thousand strings of cash.

sentences.zh: 惟良子　攸緒攸緒，惟良子也。

translations.literal: = You Xu = You Xu was a son of Weiliang.
translations.idiomatic: You Xu. You Xu was a son of Weiliang.

sentences.zh: 少有志行。

translations.literal: From youth he had ambition and conduct.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he showed purpose and integrity.

sentences.zh: 天授中封安平郡王，歷遷殿中監，出為揚州大都督府長史。

translations.literal: During Tianshou he was enfeoffed as Prince of Anping Commandery; he successively rose to Director of the Palace Administration; he went out as Chief Administrator of the Yangzhou Grand Protectorate.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianshou era he was made Prince of Anping Commandery, served as director of the palace administration, and was appointed chief administrator of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 聖歷中，棄官隱於嵩山，以琴書藥餌為務。

translations.literal: During Shenglì, he abandoned office and hid on Mount Song, making the zither, books, and medicinal preparations his occupation.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shenglì era he quit office and withdrew to Mount Song, devoting himself to music, study, and medicine.

sentences.zh: 中宗即位，以車安備禮徵之，降書曰：

translations.literal: When Zhongzong ascended the throne, he summoned him with carriage, security, and full ceremonial rites, issuing an edict that said:
translations.idiomatic: When Zhongzong took the throne, he summoned You Xu with a carriage and full honors and issued an imperial letter saying:

sentences.zh: 攸緒應召至都，授太子賓客。

translations.literal: You Xu answered the summons and arrived at the capital; he was appointed Mentor to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: You Xu answered the summons to the capital and was appointed mentor to the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 尋請歸嵩山，制從之，令京官五品已上餞送於定鼎門外。

translations.literal: Soon he requested to return to Mount Song; an edict granted this, ordering capital officials of fifth rank and above to provide a farewell send-off outside the Dingding Gate.
translations.idiomatic: He soon asked to return to Mount Song; the emperor agreed and ordered officials of fifth rank and above to escort him out through the Dingding Gate.

sentences.zh: 及三思、延秀等構逆，諸武多坐誅戮，唯攸緒以隱居不預其禍，時論美之。

translations.literal: When Sansi, Yanxiu, and others plotted treason, many of the Wu clan were condemned and executed; only You Xu, through reclusion, did not share in their calamity — contemporary opinion praised him.
translations.idiomatic: When Sansi, Yanxiu, and others rose in treason, most of the Wu clan were executed; You Xu alone escaped disaster through reclusion, and contemporaries praised his foresight.

sentences.zh: 睿宗即位，又降敕曰：「頃以賊臣結黨，后族擅權，扇動宮闈，肆行鴆毒。

translations.literal: When Ruizong ascended the throne, he again issued an edict saying: "Recently, because traitorous ministers formed factions and the empress's clan usurped power, stirring up turmoil in the inner palace and wantonly practicing poison.
translations.idiomatic: When Ruizong took the throne, he issued another edict: "Recently traitorous ministers formed factions, the empress's clan seized power, stirred turmoil in the inner palace, and poison ran rampant.

sentences.zh: 靈祇所感，奸惡伏誅；

translations.literal: Moved by spirits and gods, the wicked were secretly executed;
translations.idiomatic: Heaven and earth moved, and the wicked were destroyed;

sentences.zh: 今得宗社乂安，天地交泰。

translations.literal: Now the altars of state have attained peace and order; heaven and earth are in harmonious flourishing.
translations.idiomatic: Now the altars of state are secure and heaven and earth are at peace.

sentences.zh: 卿久厭簪紱，早慕林泉，守道不回，見幾而作，興言高尚，有足嘉稱。

translations.literal: You have long wearied of official insignia, early yearned for forests and springs, held to the Way without turning back, saw the pivot and acted — speaking of lofty conduct, there is ample reason for praise.
translations.idiomatic: You long ago wearied of office and yearned for the wilderness; steadfast in the Way, you saw danger and acted in time. Such lofty conduct deserves praise.

sentences.zh: 但怒用不遷，罪無相及，為善有驗，卿之謂與！

translations.literal: But anger does not shift to the worthy; guilt does not extend to others; doing good finds verification — is this not your case!
translations.idiomatic: Yet wrath did not touch the worthy, guilt did not extend to you, and virtue was rewarded — was this not true in your case?

sentences.zh: 或慮驚疑，故令慰謝。」

translations.literal: Perhaps fearing alarm and doubt, I therefore send this consolation and apology."
translations.idiomatic: Lest you remain alarmed or doubtful, I send this reassurance."

sentences.zh: 其見重如此。

translations.literal: Such was the esteem in which he was held.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the esteem in which he was held.

sentences.zh: 尋徵為太子賓客，不就，

translations.literal: Soon he was summoned as Mentor to the Heir Apparent; he did not accept,
translations.idiomatic: He was soon summoned again as mentor to the heir apparent but declined.

sentences.zh: 攸緒又請就廬山居止，制不許。

translations.literal: You Xu again requested to dwell on Mount Lu; an edict did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: You Xu then asked to live on Mount Lu, but the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 仍令州縣數加存問，不令外人侵擾。

translations.literal: Still he ordered prefectures and counties repeatedly to extend inquiries after his welfare, not permitting outsiders to molest him.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered local officials to watch over him and forbade outsiders to harass him.

sentences.zh: 十一年卒，年六十九。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he died, aged sixty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the eleventh year of Kaiyuan, at sixty-nine.

sentences.zh: 薛懷義者，京兆鄠縣人，本姓馮，名小寶。

translations.literal: Xue Huaiyi was a man of Hu County in Jingzhao; his original surname was Feng and his given name Xiaobao.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Huaiyi was from Hu County in Jingzhao, originally named Feng Xiaobao.

sentences.zh: 以鬻臺貨為業，偉形神，有膂力，為市於洛陽，得幸於千金公主侍兒。

translations.literal: He made his living selling platform goods; his form and spirit were imposing; he had physical strength; he plied his trade in Luoyang and gained favor with a serving girl of Princess Qianjin.
translations.idiomatic: He made his living as a peddler; tall and powerfully built, he sold his wares in Luoyang and won the favor of a maid in Princess Qianjin's household.

sentences.zh: 公主知之，入宮言曰：「小寶有非常材用，可以近侍。」

translations.literal: The princess learned of this; entering the palace she said: "Xiaobao has extraordinary talent and ability — he may serve close at hand."
translations.idiomatic: When the princess learned of him, she entered the palace and said, "Xiaobao has exceptional gifts and should serve at court."

sentences.zh: 因得召見，恩遇日深。

translations.literal: Thereupon he received a summons to audience; grace and favor daily deepened.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to audience, and imperial favor toward him grew daily.

sentences.zh: 則天欲隱其跡，便於出入禁中，乃度為僧。

translations.literal: Zetian wished to conceal his tracks for convenient entry and exit within the forbidden precincts; she therefore had him tonsured as a monk.
translations.idiomatic: To conceal his visits to the inner palace, Zetian had him ordained as a monk.

sentences.zh: 又以懷義非士族，乃改姓薛，令與太平公主婿薛紹合族，令紹以季父事之。

translations.literal: Also because Huaiyi was not of the gentry clans, she changed his surname to Xue, had him join clan with Princess Taiping's son-in-law Xue Shao, and ordered Shao to treat him as a paternal uncle by marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Because he was not of a gentry clan, she gave him the surname Xue, had him incorporated into Princess Taiping's son-in-law Xue Shao's clan, and ordered Shao to treat him as a younger uncle.

sentences.zh: 自是與洛陽大德僧法明、處一、惠儼、稜行、感德、感知、靜軌、宣政等在內道場念誦。

translations.literal: From this he together with the great virtue monks of Luoyang — Faming, Chuyi, Huiyan, Lengxing, Gande, Ganzhī, Jinggui, and Xuanzheng — chanted sutras in the inner Buddhist chapel.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter he chanted sutras in the inner chapel with Luoyang's senior monks Faming, Chuyi, Huiyan, Lengxing, Gande, Ganzhī, Jinggui, and Xuanzheng.

sentences.zh: 懷義出入乘廄馬，中官侍從，諸武朝貴，匍匐禮謁，人間呼為薛師。

translations.literal: Huaiyi when going in and out rode stable horses; eunuch attendants followed; the Wu clan and court nobles prostrated themselves in reverence; among the people he was called Master Xue.
translations.idiomatic: He rode imperial horses attended by eunuchs; Wu clansmen and court nobles prostrated themselves before him; people called him Master Xue.

sentences.zh: 垂拱初，說則天於故洛陽城西修故白馬寺，懷義自護作。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chuigong, he persuaded Zetian to restore the old White Horse Temple west of old Luoyang city; Huaiyi personally supervised the construction.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Chuigong era he persuaded Zetian to rebuild the old White Horse Temple west of Luoyang, and personally supervised the work.

sentences.zh: 寺成，自為寺主。

translations.literal: When the temple was completed, he made himself its abbot.
translations.idiomatic: When it was finished, he made himself abbot.

sentences.zh: 頗恃恩狂蹶，其下犯法，人不敢言。

translations.literal: He quite relied on favor and was wildly arrogant; when his subordinates violated the law, people did not dare speak.
translations.idiomatic: Drunk on imperial favor, he grew wildly arrogant; no one dared report the crimes of his followers.

sentences.zh: 右臺御史馮思勖屢以法劾之；

translations.literal: Right Censor Feng Siyou repeatedly impeached him according to law;
translations.idiomatic: Right censor Feng Siyou repeatedly impeached him under the law;

sentences.zh: 懷義遇勖於途，令從者毆之，幾死。

translations.literal: Huaiyi encountered You on the road and ordered followers to beat him — he nearly died.
translations.idiomatic: Huaiyi met You on the road and had his followers beat him nearly to death.

sentences.zh: 又於建春門內敬愛寺別造殿宇，改名佛授記寺，

translations.literal: He also separately built halls within Jing'ai Temple inside the Jianchun Gate, renaming it Foshouji Temple,
translations.idiomatic: He also built a separate hall within Jing'ai Temple inside the Jianchun Gate and renamed it Foshouji Temple.

sentences.zh: 拆乾元殿，於其地造明堂，懷義充使督作。

translations.literal: the Qianyuan Hall was dismantled; on its site the Bright Hall was built; Huaiyi served as commissioner to supervise construction.
translations.idiomatic: The Qianyuan Hall was demolished and the Bright Hall erected on its site, with Huaiyi appointed commissioner to supervise the work.

sentences.zh: 凡役數萬人，曳一大木千人，置號頭，頭一㘚，千人齊和。

translations.literal: In all, several tens of thousands of men were conscripted; dragging one great log took a thousand men; a chant-leader was appointed — at the leader's one shout, a thousand men harmonized together.
translations.idiomatic: Tens of thousands were conscripted; a thousand men hauled each great log, a foreman calling the chant to keep them in rhythm.

sentences.zh: 明堂大屋凡三層，計高二百尺。

translations.literal: The Bright Hall's great structure had three tiers in all, totaling two hundred feet in height.
translations.idiomatic: The Bright Hall rose three stories to a height of two hundred feet.

sentences.zh: 又於明堂北起天堂，廣袤亞於明堂。

translations.literal: Also north of the Bright Hall the Hall of Paradise was raised; its breadth and length were second only to the Bright Hall.
translations.idiomatic: North of the Bright Hall he raised the Hall of Paradise, slightly smaller in scale.

sentences.zh: 懷義以功拜左威衛大將軍，封梁國公。

translations.literal: Huaiyi for his merit was appointed General of the Left Weiwu Guard and enfeoffed as Duke of Liang State.
translations.idiomatic: For his service Huaiyi was made general of the Left Weiwu Guard and enfeoffed as Duke of Liang.

sentences.zh: 永昌中，突厥默啜犯邊，以懷義為清平道大總管，率軍擊之，至單於臺，刻石紀功而還。

translations.literal: During Yongchang, the Türk Khagan Mo-chuo invaded the border; Huaiyi was made Grand Commander of the Qingping Circuit, led troops to strike him, reached the Chanyu Terrace, carved stone to record merit, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongchang era, when the Türk khagan Mo-chuo raided the frontier, Huaiyi was made grand commander of the Qingping circuit, marched against him to the Chanyu Terrace, carved a victory stele, and returned.

sentences.zh: 加輔國大將軍，進右衛大將軍，改封鄂國公、柱國，賜帛二千段。

translations.literal: He was additionally made General Who Assists the State, advanced to General of the Right Guard, changed to Duke of E State and Pillar of the State, granted two thousand bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to general who assists the state, then general of the Right Guard, made Duke of E and pillar of the state, and given two thousand bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 懷義與法明等造《大雲經》，陳符命，言則天是彌勒下生，作閻浮提主，唐氏合微。

translations.literal: Huaiyi together with Faming and others fabricated the Scripture of Great Cloud, setting forth portents, saying Zetian was Maitreya descended to birth, ruler of Jambudvīpa, and the Tang house should wane.
translations.idiomatic: Huaiyi and Faming forged the Scripture of Great Cloud, proclaiming that Zetian was Maitreya incarnate, lord of this world, and that the Tang dynasty's mandate was spent.

sentences.zh: 故則天革命稱周，懷義與法明等九人並封縣公，賜物有差，皆賜紫袈娑、銀龜袋。

translations.literal: Therefore Zetian changed the dynasty and proclaimed Zhou; Huaiyi and Faming and nine men altogether were enfeoffed as county dukes; gifts were granted in differing amounts; all were given purple kashaya robes and silver tortoise pouches.
translations.idiomatic: When Zetian seized power and proclaimed the Zhou dynasty, Huaiyi, Faming, and seven others were all enfeoffed as county dukes with gifts of purple robes and silver tortoise pouches.

sentences.zh: 其偽《大雲經》頒於天下寺，各藏一本，令升高座講說。

translations.literal: The forged Scripture of Great Cloud was promulgated to temples throughout the realm; each kept one copy, ordered to ascend the high seat and expound it.
translations.idiomatic: The forged scripture was distributed to every temple in the empire, each ordered to keep a copy and preach it from the high seat.

sentences.zh: 則天將革命，誅殺宗屬諸王，唯千金公主以巧媚善進奉獨存；

translations.literal: When Zetian was about to change the dynasty, she executed and killed clansmen and princes; only Princess Qianjin, through skillful flattery and adept tribute, alone survived;
translations.idiomatic: As Zetian prepared to seize the throne and slaughter the imperial clan, only Princess Qianjin survived through clever flattery and generous tribute;

sentences.zh: 抗疏請以則天為母，因得曲加恩寵，改邑號為延安大長公主，加實封，賜姓武氏。

translations.literal: she submitted a memorial requesting to take Zetian as mother; thereby she received special additional grace and favor — her fief title was changed to Great Eldest Princess of Yan'an, she received additional taxable fief, and was granted the surname Wu.
translations.idiomatic: she memorialized to acknowledge Zetian as her mother, won extraordinary favor, was made Great Eldest Princess of Yan'an with additional fiefs, and given the Wu surname.

sentences.zh: 以子克乂娶魏王武承嗣女，內門參問，不限早晚，見則盡歡，

translations.literal: Because her son Keyi married the daughter of Prince of Wei Wu Chengsi, she visited within the inner gates without restriction morning or evening; whenever she appeared, complete merriment ensued,
translations.idiomatic: Her son Keyi married Wu Chengsi's daughter; she visited the inner palace without restriction and was always received with full hospitality.

sentences.zh: 默啜復犯塞，又以懷義為代北道行軍大總管，以李多祚、蘇宏暉為將。

translations.literal: Mo-chuo again invaded the frontier; Huaiyi was again made Grand Commander of the Daibei Circuit campaign army, with Li Duozuo and Su Honghui as generals.
translations.idiomatic: When Mo-chuo raided again, Huaiyi was made grand commander of the Daibei campaign army, with Li Duozuo and Su Honghui as his generals.

sentences.zh: 未行，改朔方道行軍大總管，以內史李昭德為行軍長史，鳳閣侍郎、平章事蘇味道為行軍司馬，契苾明、曹仁師、沙咤忠義等十八將軍以討之。

translations.literal: Before departing, he was changed to Grand Commander of the Shuofang Circuit campaign army; Inner Scribe Li Zhaode was made campaign Chief Administrator; Associate Administrator of the Phoenix Pavilion and Co-Director of State Su Weidao was made campaign Chief of Staff; Qibi Ming, Cao Renshi, Shazha Zhongyi, and eighteen generals were to suppress the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could march, his command was changed to grand commander of the Shuofang campaign army; Li Zhaode was chief administrator, Su Weidao chief of staff, and Qibi Ming, Cao Renshi, Shazha Zhongyi, and eighteen other generals joined the expedition.

sentences.zh: 未行虜退，乃止。

translations.literal: Before departing the barbarians withdrew; the campaign was then halted.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy withdrew before the army marched, and the campaign was cancelled.

sentences.zh: 懷義後厭入宮中，多居白馬寺，刺血畫大像，選有膂力白丁度為僧，數滿千人。

translations.literal: Later Huaiyi grew weary of entering the palace; he mostly stayed at White Horse Temple, drawing a great image in his own blood; he selected strong commoners and tonsured them as monks, the number reaching a full thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Huaiyi later tired of the palace and spent most of his time at White Horse Temple, painting a great icon in his own blood and ordaining a thousand muscular commoners as monks.

sentences.zh: 侍御史周矩疑其奸，奏請劾之，不許。

translations.literal: Attending Censor Zhou Ju suspected his misconduct and memorialized requesting impeachment; this was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Attending censor Zhou Ju suspected wrongdoing and requested permission to investigate, but was refused.

sentences.zh: 固請之，則天曰：「卿且退，朕即令去。」

translations.literal: He firmly requested again; Zetian said: "You withdraw for now; I shall soon have him go to you."
translations.idiomatic: When he pressed again, Zetian said, "Withdraw for now; I shall send him to you shortly."

sentences.zh: 矩至臺，薛師亦至，乘馬蹋階而下，便坦腹於床。

translations.literal: Ju arrived at the censorate; Master Xue also arrived, riding his horse trampling down the steps, then baring his belly on a couch.
translations.idiomatic: At the censorate Master Xue appeared, rode his horse down the steps, and sprawled bare-bellied on a couch.

sentences.zh: 矩召臺吏，將按之，遽乘馬而去。

translations.literal: Ju summoned censorate clerks, about to investigate him; he suddenly mounted his horse and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Ju called clerks to question him, but Huaiyi remounted and rode off.

sentences.zh: 矩具以聞，則天曰：「此道人風病，不可苦問。

translations.literal: Ju reported the full matter; Zetian said: "This monk has wind disease — he cannot be harshly questioned.
translations.idiomatic: Ju reported everything; Zetian said, "This monk has a palsy; he cannot be questioned harshly.

sentences.zh: 所度僧任卿勘當。」

translations.literal: The monks he ordained — you may investigate and judge them."
translations.idiomatic: Investigate the monks he ordained as you see fit."

sentences.zh: 矩按之，窮其狀以聞，諸僧悉配遠州。

translations.literal: Ju investigated them, exhaustively determining the facts and reporting; all the monks were banished to distant prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Ju did so, established the facts, and reported; all the monks were exiled to distant prefectures.

sentences.zh: 遷矩天官員外郎，竟為薛師所構，下獄，免官。

translations.literal: Ju was transferred to Assistant Director in the Ministry of Personnel; in the end he was framed by Master Xue, thrown into prison, and stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: Ju was promoted to assistant director in the Ministry of Personnel but was eventually framed by Master Xue, imprisoned, and dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 後有御醫沈南璆得幸，薛師恩漸衰，恨怒頗甚。

translations.literal: Later there was imperial physician Shen Nan'yu who gained favor; Master Xue's grace gradually declined; hatred and anger were quite great.
translations.idiomatic: Later the imperial physician Shen Nan'yu won the empress's favor, and Huaiyi's influence waned; he grew bitter and furious.

sentences.zh: 證聖中，乃焚明堂、天堂，並為灰燼，則天愧而隱之，又令懷義充使督作。

translations.literal: In the Zhengsheng era he burned the Bright Hall and Paradise, both becoming ashes; Zetian was ashamed and concealed it, and again had Huaiyi serve as commissioner supervising construction.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhengsheng reign he burned the Bright Hall and Paradise to ashes; Zetian, ashamed, kept it quiet and again put Huaiyi in charge of rebuilding.

sentences.zh: 乃於明堂下置九州鼎，鑄銅為十二屬形象，置於本辰位，皆高一丈，懷義率人作號頭安置之。

translations.literal: Then below the Bright Hall he placed the Nine Provinces cauldrons, casting copper into images of the twelve zodiac signs, placing them in their proper earthly-branch positions, each one zhang high; Huaiyi led men as foremen to install them.
translations.idiomatic: Below the Bright Hall he set up the Nine Provinces cauldrons and cast copper figures of the twelve zodiac animals, each a zhang tall, placed in their proper positions; Huaiyi led work crews to install them.

sentences.zh: 其後益驕倨，則天惡之，令太平公主擇膂力婦人數十，密防慮之。

translations.literal: Afterward he grew increasingly arrogant and haughty; Zetian detested him and had Princess Taiping select several dozen strong women to secretly guard against him.
translations.idiomatic: He grew ever more arrogant; Zetian loathed him and had Princess Taiping choose several dozen muscular women to watch him in secret.

sentences.zh: 人有發其陰謀者，太平公主乳母張夫人令壯士縛而縊殺之，以輦車載屍送白馬寺。

translations.literal: When someone exposed his secret plots, Princess Taiping's wet nurse Lady Zhang had strong men bind and strangle him; a palanquin carriage transported the corpse to White Horse Temple.
translations.idiomatic: When his secret plots were exposed, Princess Taiping's wet nurse Lady Zhang had him bound and strangled; his corpse was carried by carriage to White Horse Temple.

sentences.zh: 其侍者僧徒，皆流竄遠惡處。

translations.literal: His attendant monk followers were all exiled to distant harsh places.
translations.idiomatic: His attendant monks were all banished to remote, harsh regions.

sentences.zh: 韋溫

translations.literal: = Wei Wen =
translations.idiomatic: = Wei Wen =

sentences.zh: 韋溫，中宗韋庶人從父兄也。

translations.literal: Wei Wen was a paternal cousin of Empress Wei, consort of Zhongzong.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Wen was a paternal cousin of Empress Wei, consort of Emperor Zhongzong.

sentences.zh: 父玄儼，高宗末官至許州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Xuanran, at the end of Gaozong's reign reached the post of prefect of Xu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xuanran served as prefect of Xu Prefecture in the final years of Gaozong's reign.

sentences.zh: 玄儼弟玄貞，初為普州參軍，以女為皇太子妃，擢拜豫州刺史。

translations.literal: Xuanran's younger brother Xuanzhen, initially military aide of Pu Prefecture, because his daughter became crown prince's consort, was promoted and appointed prefect of Yu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanran's younger brother Xuanzhen had been a staff officer in Pu Prefecture; when his daughter became crown prince's consort, he was promoted to prefect of Yu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 中宗嗣位，妃為后。

translations.literal: When Zhongzong succeeded, the consort became empress.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhongzong took the throne, she became empress.

sentences.zh: 及帝降為廬陵王，玄貞配流欽州而死。

translations.literal: When the emperor was demoted to Prince of Luling, Xuanzhen was banished to Qin Prefecture and died there.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor was reduced to Prince of Luling, Xuanzhen was exiled to Qin Prefecture and died there.

sentences.zh: 后母崔氏，為欽州首領寧承兄弟所殺。

translations.literal: The empress's mother, the Cui clan, was killed by the brothers of Ning Cheng, a Qin Prefecture chieftain.
translations.idiomatic: The empress's mother, Lady Cui, was killed by the brothers of Ning Cheng, a chieftain in Qin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 玄貞有四子：洵、浩、洞、泚，亦死於容州。

translations.literal: Xuanzhen had four sons: Xun, Hao, Dong, and Ci; they also died at Rong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzhen had four sons—Xun, Hao, Dong, and Ci—who also died in Rong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 后二妹，逃竄獲免，間行歸長安。

translations.literal: The empress's two younger sisters fled and escaped, traveling by hidden routes back to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: The empress's two younger sisters fled, evaded capture, and made their way back to Chang'an by secret paths.

sentences.zh: 及中宗復位，韋氏復為皇后。

translations.literal: When Zhongzong was restored, the Wei clan again became empress.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhongzong was restored to the throne, Lady Wei was again made empress.

sentences.zh: 其日，追贈玄貞為上洛郡王。

translations.literal: That day, Xuanzhen was posthumously ennobled as Prince of Shangluo Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: That same day Xuanzhen was posthumously ennobled as Prince of Shangluo.

sentences.zh: 左拾遺賈虛己上疏諫曰：「孔子曰：『惟名與器，不可以假人。』

translations.literal: Left Reminder Jia Xuji submitted a memorial remonstrating, saying: "Confucius said: 'Titles and instruments of office may not be lent to others.
translations.idiomatic: Left Reminder Jia Xuji submitted a memorial of remonstrance: "Confucius said, 'Titles and the instruments of office must not be lent to others.

sentences.zh: 且非李氏而王，自古盟書所棄。

translations.literal: Moreover, ennobling non-Li clans as kings has been rejected in oaths since antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, making non-Li clans kings has been forbidden in oaths since antiquity.

sentences.zh: 今陛下創制謀始，垂範將來，為皇王令圖，子孫明鏡。

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty is founding institutions and planning from the start, establishing a model for the future—a fine blueprint for kings and a mirror for posterity.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is now founding institutions and setting a pattern for generations—a model for sovereigns and a mirror for your descendants.

sentences.zh: 匡復未幾，后族有私，臣雖庸愚，尚知未可；

translations.literal: Not long after restoration, the empress's clan is granted private favor; though I am dull and ignorant, I still know this is unwise;
translations.idiomatic: Barely restored, the empress's kin already receive private favors; though I am dull, I know this cannot stand;

sentences.zh: 史官執簡，必是直書。

translations.literal: the historiographers with their bamboo slips will surely record it straight.
translations.idiomatic: the historiographers will surely set it down without flattery.

sentences.zh: 今萬姓颙然，聞一善令，莫不途歌里頌，延頸向風，欣然慕化，日恐不及。

translations.literal: Now the myriad people look up expectantly; hearing one good decree, none fail to sing it on the roads and praise it in villages, craning their necks toward the good wind, gladly admiring reform, fearing each day they may not catch up.
translations.idiomatic: The people look up in hope; at every good decree they sing in the streets and praise in the lanes, turning toward reform with joy, afraid only of falling behind.

sentences.zh: 陛下奈何行私惠，使樵夫議之。

translations.literal: How can Your Majesty bestow private favor and let woodcutters comment on it?
translations.idiomatic: How can Your Majesty grant private favors and let woodcutters gossip about it?

sentences.zh: 即先朝贈太原王，殷鑒不遠。

translations.literal: The previous dynasty's ennoblement of the Prince of Taiyuan is a warning not far off.
translations.idiomatic: The previous dynasty's ennoblement of the Prince of Taiyuan is a warning close at hand.

sentences.zh: 同雲生於膚寸，尋木起於蘗栽，誠可惜也。

translations.literal: Clouds of the same kind arise from a hand's breadth; tall trees grow from stump shoots—truly a pity.
translations.idiomatic: Storm clouds gather from a patch no wider than a hand; great trees spring from a stump—what a waste to let small beginnings grow into ruin.

sentences.zh: 渙汗既行，難改成命，臣望請皇后抗表固辭，使天下知弘讓之風，彤管著沖謙之德，是則巍巍聖鑒，無得而稱。」

translations.literal: The imperial decree has already gone forth and is hard to revoke; I hope the empress may submit a memorial firmly declining, so the realm knows the spirit of generous yielding, and the red brush records her modest virtue—then Your Majesty's lofty wisdom would be beyond praise."
translations.idiomatic: The decree has gone forth and cannot easily be withdrawn; I beg that the empress submit a memorial firmly declining, so the realm may know the virtue of yielding and history record her modesty—then Your Majesty's wisdom would be beyond praise."

sentences.zh: 疏奏不省。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted but not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was submitted and ignored.

sentences.zh: 尋又追贈玄貞為太師、雍州牧、益州大都督；

translations.literal: Soon Xuanzhen was again posthumously honored as Grand Preceptor, Governor of Yong Province, and Grand Protector-General of Yi Province;
translations.idiomatic: Soon Xuanzhen was again posthumously honored as Grand Preceptor, Governor of Yong Province, and Grand Protector-General of Yi Province;

sentences.zh: 玄儼為特進、并州大都督、魯國公。

translations.literal: Xuanran as Special Advancement, Grand Protector-General of Bing Province, and Duke of Lu.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanran as Special Advancement, Grand Protector-General of Bing Province, and Duke of Lu.

sentences.zh: 遣使迎玄貞及崔氏喪柩歸京師。

translations.literal: Envoys were sent to bring back the coffins of Xuanzhen and Lady Cui to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys were dispatched to bring the coffins of Xuanzhen and Lady Cui back to the capital.

sentences.zh: 又遣廣州都督周仁軌率兵討斬寧承兄弟，以其首祭於崔氏。

translations.literal: Also dispatched Guangzhou Protector-General Zhou Rengui at the head of troops to attack and behead the Ning Cheng brothers, using their heads to sacrifice before Lady Cui.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent Guangzhou Protector-General Zhou Rengui with troops to attack and behead the Ning Cheng brothers, offering their heads before Lady Cui's coffin.

sentences.zh: 擢拜仁軌左羽林大將軍，賜爵汝南郡公，食實封五百戶。

translations.literal: Rengui was promoted to Left General of the Feathered Forest Guard, granted the title Duke of Runan Commandery, with five hundred taxable households.
translations.idiomatic: Rengui was promoted to Left General of the Feathered Forest Guard, enfeoffed as Duke of Runan, with an estate of five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 及玄貞等柩將至，上與后登長樂宮，望喪而泣。

translations.literal: When the coffins of Xuanzhen and the others were about to arrive, the emperor and empress ascended Changle Palace, gazing toward the funeral procession and weeping.
translations.idiomatic: As the coffins of Xuanzhen and the others neared the capital, the emperor and empress climbed Changle Palace, gazed toward the procession, and wept.

sentences.zh: 加贈玄貞為酆王，謚曰文獻，仍號其廟曰褒德，陵曰榮先。

translations.literal: Xuanzhen was further posthumously ennobled as Prince of Feng, with posthumous title Wenxian; his temple was named Baode and his tomb Rongxian.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzhen was further ennobled posthumously as Prince of Feng, with the posthumous name Wenxian; his temple was called Baode and his tomb Rongxian.

sentences.zh: 各置官員，並給戶一百人守衛灑掃。

translations.literal: Officials were appointed for each, and one hundred households were assigned to guard and sweep clean.
translations.idiomatic: Officials were appointed for each site, and one hundred households were assigned to guard and maintain them.

sentences.zh: 又贈玄貞子洵為吏部尚書、汝南郡王，浩太常卿、武陵郡王，洞衛尉卿、淮南郡王，泚太僕卿、上蔡郡王，亦遣使迎其喪柩於京師。

translations.literal: Also posthumously honored Xuanzhen's sons: Xun as Minister of Personnel and Prince of Runan; Hao as Minister of Ceremonies and Prince of Wuling; Dong as Minister of the Guard and Prince of Huainan; Ci as Minister of the Stud and Prince of Shangcai—and envoys were also sent to bring their coffins to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzhen's sons were also honored posthumously: Xun as Minister of Personnel and Prince of Runan; Hao as Minister of Ceremonies and Prince of Wuling; Dong as Minister of the Guard and Prince of Huainan; Ci as Minister of the Stud and Prince of Shangcai—and envoys were sent to bring their coffins to the capital.

sentences.zh: 溫，神龍中累遷禮部尚書，封魯國公。

translations.literal: Wen, during the Shenlong era, was repeatedly promoted to Minister of Rites and enfeoffed as Duke of Lu.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shenlong era Wen rose to Minister of Rites and was enfeoffed as Duke of Lu.

sentences.zh: 弟湑，左羽林將軍，封曹國公。

translations.literal: His younger brother Xu was Left General of the Feathered Forest Guard, enfeoffed as Duke of Cao.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Xu was Left General of the Feathered Forest Guard and Duke of Cao.

sentences.zh: 后妹夫陸頌為國子祭酒，馮太和為太常少卿，太和尋卒，又適嗣虢王邕。

translations.literal: The empress's brothers-in-law Lu Song served as Chancellor of the Directorate of Education, and Feng Taihe as Vice Minister of Ceremonies; Taihe soon died, and [his widow] then married Prince of Guo Heir Yong.
translations.idiomatic: The empress's brothers-in-law Lu Song became Chancellor of the Directorate of Education and Feng Taihe Vice Minister of Ceremonies; Taihe soon died, and his widow then married Heir Apparent Yong of Guo.

sentences.zh: 湑子捷，尚成安公主，溫從祖弟濯，尚定安公主，皆拜駙馬都尉，

translations.literal: Xu's son Jie married Princess Cheng'an; Wen's third-cousin Zhuo married Princess Ding'an—both were appointed Commandants of the Escort,
translations.idiomatic: Xu's son Jie married Princess Cheng'an, and Wen's third cousin Zhuo married Princess Ding'an; both were made imperial sons-in-law,

sentences.zh: 溫遷太子少保、同中書門下三品，仍遙授揚州大都督。

translations.literal: Wen was promoted to Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent, Co-Chancellor under the Secretariat and Chancellery, and concurrently given the distant appointment of Grand Protector-General of Yang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wen was promoted to junior mentor of the heir, chancellor of the second rank, and titular grand protector-general of Yang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 溫等既居榮要，燻灼朝野，時人比之武氏。

translations.literal: Once Wen and the others held glorious positions, they scorched court and countryside; contemporaries compared them to the Wu clan.
translations.idiomatic: Once Wen and his kin held power, their glare scorched court and countryside; people compared them to the Wu clan.

sentences.zh: 湑及陸頌相次病卒，賻贈甚厚。

translations.literal: Xu and Lu Song successively died of illness; mourning gifts were very generous.
translations.idiomatic: Xu and Lu Song died of illness in succession; the mourning gifts were lavish.

sentences.zh: 及中宗崩，后令溫總知內外兵馬，守援宮掖。

translations.literal: When Zhongzong died, the empress ordered Wen to oversee all internal and external military forces and defend the palace.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhongzong died, the empress put Wen in charge of all palace and field forces to defend the inner quarters.

sentences.zh: 又引從子播、族弟璇、弟捷、濯等，分掌屯營及左右羽林軍。

translations.literal: She also brought in his nephew Bo, clansman cousin Xuan, younger brother Jie, Zhuo, and others to separately command encampment troops and the Left and Right Feathered Forest Guards.
translations.idiomatic: She also installed his nephew Bo, clansman Xuan, younger brother Jie, Zhuo, and others to command encampment troops and the Left and Right Feathered Forest Guards.

sentences.zh: 臨淄王討韋氏，溫等皆坐斬，宗族無少長皆死，語在《韋庶人傳》。

translations.literal: When Prince of Linzi attacked the Wei clan, Wen and the others were all executed; the entire clan, young and old, perished—the account is in the "Biography of Empress Wei."
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Linzi moved against the Wei faction, Wen and the rest were executed; the whole clan, young and old, was wiped out—the full account is in the Biography of Empress Wei.

sentences.zh: 睿宗即位，仍令削平玄貞及洵等墳墓。

translations.literal: When Ruizong ascended, he again ordered the leveling of the tombs of Xuanzhen, Xun, and the others.
translations.idiomatic: When Ruizong took the throne, he ordered the tombs of Xuanzhen, Xun, and the others leveled.

sentences.zh: 王仁皎

translations.literal: = Wang Renjiao =
translations.idiomatic: = Wang Renjiao =

sentences.zh: 王仁皎，玄宗王庶人父也。

translations.literal: Wang Renjiao was the father of Consort Wang of Emperor Xuanzong.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Renjiao was the father of Emperor Xuanzong's consort Wang.

sentences.zh: 景龍中，官至長上果毅。

translations.literal: During the Jinglong era, he reached the post of Changshang Brave Captain.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jinglong era he rose to the rank of Changshang Brave Captain.

sentences.zh: 玄宗即位，以后父，歷將作大匠、太僕卿，遷開府儀同三司，封祁國公。

translations.literal: When Xuanzong ascended, as the empress's father he served successively as Director of Palace Works, Minister of the Stud, was promoted to Grand General of the State with Extraordinary Honors, and enfeoffed as Duke of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuanzong took the throne, as the empress's father he served as Director of Palace Works and Minister of the Stud, then rose to Grand General of the State with Extraordinary Honors and was enfeoffed as Duke of Qi.

sentences.zh: 仁皎不預朝政，但厚自奉養，積子女財貨而已。

translations.literal: Renjiao did not participate in court politics, but lavishly indulged himself, amassing sons, daughters, wealth, and goods—that was all.
translations.idiomatic: Renjiao stayed out of politics and lived in luxury, hoarding wealth and raising a large family—that was all he did.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈太尉，官供葬事。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously honored as Grand Commandant; the government provided the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: When he died he was posthumously honored as Grand Commandant, and the state provided his funeral.

sentences.zh: 柩車既發，上於望春亭遙望之，令張說為其碑文，玄宗親書石焉。

translations.literal: When the funeral procession set out, the emperor watched from afar at Wangchun Pavilion, had Zhang Yue compose his epitaph, and Xuanzong personally inscribed the stone.
translations.idiomatic: When the coffin departed, the emperor watched from Wangchun Pavilion, had Zhang Yue write the epitaph, and personally inscribed the stone.

sentences.zh: 子守一。

translations.literal: His son Shouyi.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Shouyi.

sentences.zh: 守一與后雙生。

translations.literal: Shouyi and the empress were twins.
translations.idiomatic: Shouyi and the empress were twins.

sentences.zh: 守一與玄宗有舊，及上登極，以清陽公主妻之。

translations.literal: Shouyi had old ties with Xuanzong; when the emperor took the throne, he gave him Princess Qingyang in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Shouyi had known Xuanzong since youth; when the emperor took the throne, he married him to Princess Qingyang.

sentences.zh: 從討蕭至忠、岑羲等有功，自尚乘奉御遷殿中少監，特封晉國公，累轉太子少保。
