translations.literal: For merit in following the campaign against Xiao Zhizhong, Cen Xi, and others, he rose from Groom-in-Waiting to Vice Director of the Palace Domestic Service, was specially enfeoffed Duke of Jin, and was repeatedly promoted to Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: For merit in the campaign against Xiao Zhizhong and Cen Xi, he rose from groom-in-waiting to vice director of the palace service, was specially enfeoffed Duke of Jin, and eventually became junior mentor of the heir.

sentences.zh: 父卒，襲爵祁國公。

translations.literal: When his father died, he inherited the title Duke of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died, he inherited the dukedom of Qi.

sentences.zh: 十一年，坐與庶人潛通左道，左遷柳州司馬，行至藍田驛，賜死。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, for secretly communicating with the Deposed Consort through heterodox practices, he was demoted to military adjutant of Liuzhou; reaching Lantian Post, he was granted death.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he was convicted of secretly communicating with the deposed consort through sorcery, demoted to military adjutant of Liuzhou, and granted death at Lantian Post.

sentences.zh: 守一性貪鄙，積財巨萬，及籍沒其家，財帛不可勝計。

translations.literal: Shouyi was greedy and base by nature, amassing wealth in the tens of thousands; when his household was confiscated, money and silk were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Shouyi was greedy and vulgar by nature and amassed vast wealth; when his property was confiscated, the money and silk were beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 吳溆

translations.literal: = Wu Xu =
translations.idiomatic: = Wu Xu =

sentences.zh: 吳溆，章敬皇后之弟也，濮州濮陽人。

translations.literal: Wu Xu was the younger brother of Empress Zhangjing, a native of Puyang in Pu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Xu was the younger brother of Empress Zhangjing and a native of Puyang in Pu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 祖神泉，位終縣令。

translations.literal: His grandfather Shenquan ended his career as county magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Shenquan ended his career as a county magistrate.

sentences.zh: 父令珪，益州郫縣丞，

translations.literal: His father Linggui was assistant magistrate of Pi County in Yi Prefecture,
translations.idiomatic: His father Linggui was assistant magistrate of Pi County in Yi Prefecture,

sentences.zh: 代宗始封拜外族，贈神泉司徒，令珪太尉，令珪母弟前宣城令令瑤為開府儀同三司、太子家令，封濮陽郡公；

translations.literal: when Daizong first enfeoffed and appointed affinal kin, Shenquan was posthumously honored as Minister of Education; Linggui as Grand Commandant; Linggui's younger maternal half-brother, former magistrate of Xuancheng Lingyao, as Grand General with Extraordinary Honors and Household Steward of the Heir Apparent, enfeoffed Duke of Puyang Commandery;
translations.idiomatic: when Daizong first enfeoffed maternal kin, Shenquan was posthumously made Minister of Education, Linggui Grand Commandant, and Linggui's younger maternal half-brother, the former magistrate of Xuancheng Lingyao, Grand General with Extraordinary Honors and household steward of the heir, Duke of Puyang;

sentences.zh: 中郎將令瑜為開府儀同三司、太子諭德、濟陽郡公。

translations.literal: Middle General Lingyu as Grand General with Extraordinary Honors, Mentor to the Heir Apparent, Duke of Jiyang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Middle General Lingyu as Grand General with Extraordinary Honors, mentor to the heir, and Duke of Jiyang.

sentences.zh: 漵時為盛王府錄事參軍，拜開府儀同三司、太子詹事、濮陽郡公。

translations.literal: At that time Xu was Recorder of the Prince of Sheng's household; he was appointed Grand General with Extraordinary Honors, Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, and Duke of Puyang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Xu was recorder on the staff of the Prince of Sheng; he was appointed Grand General with Extraordinary Honors, grand mentor of the heir, and Duke of Puyang.

sentences.zh: 以元舅遷鴻臚少卿、金吾將軍。

translations.literal: As maternal uncle by marriage, he was promoted to Vice Director of the Court of State Ceremonies and General of the Golden Guard.
translations.idiomatic: As the empress's uncle he was promoted to vice director of the Court of State Ceremonies and general of the Golden Guard.

sentences.zh: 建中初，遷大將軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jianzhong era, he was promoted to Great General.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Jianzhong era he was promoted to great general.

sentences.zh: 漵雖居戚屬，恭遜謙和，人皆重之。

translations.literal: Though Xu was an imperial in-law, he was respectful, deferential, and modest; all held him in esteem.
translations.idiomatic: Though an imperial in-law, Xu was courteous and modest, and everyone respected him.

sentences.zh: 涇師之亂，從幸奉天，盧杞、白志貞謂德宗曰：「臣細觀硃泚心跡，必不至為戎首，佇當效順。

translations.literal: During the Jingshi mutiny, following the emperor to Fengtian, Lu Qi and Bai Zhizhen said to Dezong: "We have closely observed Zhu Ci's intentions; he will surely not become rebel leader and will soon submit.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jingshi mutiny, as the emperor fled to Fengtian, Lu Qi and Bai Zhizhen told Dezong, "We have watched Zhu Ci closely; he will surely not lead the rebellion and will soon submit.

sentences.zh: 宜擇大臣一人，入京師慰諭，以觀其心。」

translations.literal: A senior minister should be chosen to enter the capital and offer reassurance, to observe his intentions."
translations.idiomatic: Choose a senior minister to enter the capital and reassure him, and we can see where his heart lies."

sentences.zh: 上召從幸群臣言之，皆憚其行。

translations.literal: The emperor summoned the officials who had followed him and put the matter before them; all feared to go.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked the officials who had accompanied him; all shrank from the mission.

sentences.zh: 漵起奏曰：「不以臣才望無堪，臣願北行。」

translations.literal: Xu rose and submitted: "Disregarding that my talent and standing are unworthy, I am willing to go north."
translations.idiomatic: Xu rose and said, "Never mind that my talent and rank are unworthy—I am willing to go north."

sentences.zh: 德宗甚悅。

translations.literal: Dezong was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong was greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 漵退而謂人曰：「人臣食君之祿，死君之難，臨危自計，非忠也。

translations.literal: Xu withdrew and said to others: "A minister who eats the ruler's stipend should die in the ruler's peril; to calculate for oneself in crisis is not loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Xu withdrew and told others, "A minister who eats the ruler's grain should die in the ruler's peril; to weigh one's own safety in crisis is not loyalty.

sentences.zh: 吾忝戚屬，今日委身於賊，誠知必死，不欲聖情慊於無人犯難也。」

translations.literal: I am ashamed as an imperial relative; today I devote myself to the rebels, knowing I shall surely die, because I do not wish the sacred heart to be vexed that no one would brave the peril."
translations.idiomatic: I am an imperial in-law; today I throw myself among the rebels knowing I must die, because I cannot bear that the emperor should be troubled that no one would face the danger."

sentences.zh: 即日賫詔見泚，深陳上待屬之意。

translations.literal: That very day he bore the edict to see Zhu Ci and earnestly conveyed the emperor's goodwill toward his followers.
translations.idiomatic: That same day he carried the edict to Zhu Ci and earnestly conveyed the emperor's goodwill toward his followers.

sentences.zh: 時泚逆謀已定，貌雖從命，而心已異，乃留漵於客省，竟被害。

translations.literal: At that time Zhu Ci's treason was already settled; though outwardly compliant, his heart was already changed; he detained Xu in the guest lodge, and Xu was eventually killed.
translations.idiomatic: By then Zhu Ci's treason was already fixed; though he appeared to comply, his heart had turned; he detained Xu in the guest lodge, and Xu was killed.

sentences.zh: 上聞之，悲悼不已，贈太子太傅，賜其家實封二百戶，一子五品正員官，敕收城日葬事官給。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard, he grieved without end; Xu was posthumously honored as Grand Tutor to the Heir Apparent; his family was granted two hundred taxable households; one son a regular fifth-rank office; an edict ordered that on the day the city was recovered, funeral expenses would be provided by the government.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard, he grieved deeply; Xu was posthumously made Grand Tutor to the Heir Apparent, his family granted two hundred taxable households and one son a regular fifth-rank post, and an edict promised state funeral rites when the capital was recovered.

sentences.zh: 弟湊。

translations.literal: Younger brother Cou.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother was Cou.

sentences.zh: 湊，寶歷中與兄漵同日開府，授太子詹事，俱封濮陽郡公。

translations.literal: Cou, during the Baoli era on the same day as his elder brother Xu received grand general status, was appointed Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent; both were enfeoffed Dukes of Puyang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Cou, in the Baoli era, received grand general honors on the same day as his elder brother Xu and was appointed grand mentor of the heir; both were enfeoffed as Dukes of Puyang.

sentences.zh: 湊以兄弟三品，固辭太過，乞授卑官。

translations.literal: Cou, because both brothers held third rank, firmly declined as excessive and requested a lower office.
translations.idiomatic: Cou felt it excessive for both brothers to hold third rank and firmly asked for a lesser appointment.

sentences.zh: 乃以湊檢校太子賓客，兼太子家令，充十宅王使。

translations.literal: Cou was then made Acting Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, concurrently Household Steward of the Heir Apparent, and Commissioner of the Ten Princely Residences.
translations.idiomatic: He was then made acting grand mentor of the heir, concurrently household steward of the heir and commissioner of the Ten Princely Residences.

sentences.zh: 累轉左金吾衛大將軍。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Left General of the Golden Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was later promoted to left general of the Golden Guard.

sentences.zh: 湊小心謹慎，智識周敏，特承顧問，偏見委信。

translations.literal: Cou was careful and cautious, quick-witted and perceptive; he especially received imperial consultation and was singled out for trust.
translations.idiomatic: Cou was cautious and quick-witted; the emperor consulted him often and singled him out for trust.

sentences.zh: 大歷中，滑帥令狐彰、汴帥田神功相次歿於理所，時籓方兵驕，乘戎帥喪亡，人情多梗。

translations.literal: During the Dali era, the military governors of Hua (Linghu Zhang) and Bian (Tian Shengon) successively died in their jurisdictions; at the time frontier troops were arrogant; seizing on the commanders' deaths, public sentiment was much unsettled.
translations.idiomatic: In the Dali era the governors of Hua, Linghu Zhang, and Bian, Tian Shengon, died in succession at their posts; frontier troops were unruly, and with the commanders gone unrest spread.

sentences.zh: 代宗命湊銜命撫慰，至必委曲說諭，隨所欲為之奏請，皆得軍民和協，帝深重之。

translations.literal: Daizong ordered Cou on imperial commission to comfort and reassure; wherever he arrived he explained persuasively; whatever they desired he memorialized for; all achieved military-civilian harmony; the emperor valued him deeply.
translations.idiomatic: Daizong sent Cou on imperial commission to reassure them; wherever he went he spoke persuasively and memorialized whatever they asked; civil and military affairs settled, and the emperor valued him highly.

sentences.zh: 宰臣元載弄權，招致賄賂，醜跡日彰。

translations.literal: Chancellor Yuan Zai manipulated power, soliciting bribes; his shameful deeds grew daily apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Yuan Zai abused his power and took bribes; his corruption grew daily more obvious.

sentences.zh: 帝惡之，將加之法，恐左右泄漏，無與言者，唯與湊密計圖之。

translations.literal: The emperor detested him and planned to punish him by law, fearing leaks from those around him; having no one to speak with, he confided only in Cou to plot it secretly.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor hated him and planned to punish him by law, but feared leaks among his attendants; he confided in no one but Cou.

sentences.zh: 及收載於內侍省，同列王縉，其黨楊炎、王昂、韓洄、包佶、韓會等，皆當從坐籍沒。

translations.literal: When Zai was arrested in the Directorate of Palace Attendants, his colleague Wang Jin and his faction Yang Yan, Wang Ang, Han Hui, Bao Ji, Han Hui, and others were all liable for complicity and confiscation.
translations.idiomatic: When Zai was arrested in the Directorate of Palace Attendants, his colleague Wang Jin and his allies Yang Yan, Wang Ang, Han Hui, Bao Ji, Han Hui, and others were all liable to complicity and confiscation.

sentences.zh: 湊諫救百端，言「法宜從寬，縉等從坐，理不至死。

translations.literal: Cou remonstrated extensively to save them, saying "The law should be applied leniently; Jin and the others, though complicit, by right do not deserve death.
translations.idiomatic: Cou argued at length to save them: "The law should be applied with mercy; Jin and the others, though complicit, do not deserve death.

sentences.zh: 若不降以等差，一例極刑，恐虧損聖德。」

translations.literal: If there is no reduction by degrees and all receive the extreme penalty, I fear it will harm Your Majesty's virtue."
translations.idiomatic: If all are punished alike with the death penalty, I fear it will tarnish Your Majesty's virtue."

sentences.zh: 由是縉等得減死，流貶之。

translations.literal: Therefore Jin and the others had their death sentences reduced and were exiled and demoted.
translations.idiomatic: Jin and the others were spared death and exiled instead.

sentences.zh: 大歷末，丁繼母喪免。

translations.literal: At the end of the Dali era, on his stepmother's death he was dismissed to observe mourning.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Dali era he left office to mourn his stepmother.

sentences.zh: 建中初，起為右衛將軍，兼通州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianzhong he was recalled as General of the Right Guard, concurrently prefect of Tong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Jianzhong he was recalled as general of the Right Guard and prefect of Tong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 貞元初，入為太子賓客，出為福州刺史、御史中丞、福建觀察使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenyuan he entered court as Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, then went out as prefect of Fu Prefecture, Censor-in-Chief, and Commissioner of Fujian Observation.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Zhenyuan he returned as grand mentor of the heir, then went out as prefect of Fu, censor-in-chief, and Fujian observation commissioner.

sentences.zh: 為政勤儉清苦，美譽日聞。

translations.literal: In administration he was diligent, frugal, and austere; his fine reputation spread daily.
translations.idiomatic: In office he was diligent, frugal, and austere, and his reputation for integrity spread daily.

sentences.zh: 宰相竇參以私怨惡之，數加譖毀，又言湊風病，不任趨馳。

translations.literal: Chancellor Dou Can hated him for private grievances, repeatedly slandered him, and also said Cou had wind disease and could not manage hurried travel.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Dou Can bore him a private grudge, slandered him again and again, and claimed Cou suffered from paralysis and could no longer keep pace with urgent duties.

sentences.zh: 德宗召湊至京師，對於別殿，上令殿上行走，以驗其病否，由是悟參之誣，因是惡參。

translations.literal: Dezong summoned Cou to the capital, received him in a side hall, had him walk about the hall to test whether he was ill; thereby realizing Can's falsehood, and for this reason came to detest Can.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong summoned Cou to the capital and received him in a side hall, then had him walk back and forth across the hall to test his ailment. Seeing that Can had lied, the emperor turned against him.

sentences.zh: 尋以湊為陜州大都督府長史、陜虢觀察使，以代參之黨李翼。

translations.literal: Soon Cou was made chief administrator of the Shaanzhou grand protectorate and Shaan-Guo observation commissioner, replacing Can's ally Li Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Cou was soon made chief administrator of Shaanzhou and Shaan-Guo observation commissioner, replacing Can's ally Li Yi.

sentences.zh: 會劉玄佐卒，以湊檢校兵部尚書、汴州刺史、御史大夫、宣武軍節度使。

translations.literal: When Liu Xuanzuo died, Cou was made acting minister of war, prefect of Bian, censor-in-chief, and military governor of the Xuanwu Army.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Xuanzuo died, Cou was appointed acting minister of war, prefect of Bian, censor-in-chief, and military governor of the Xuanwu Army.

sentences.zh: 時汴州軍亂，殺牙將曹金岸、縣令李邁，謀立玄佐子士寧。

translations.literal: At the time Bian Prefecture troops mutinied, killed adjutant Cao Jin'an and magistrate Li Mai, and plotted to install Xuanzuo's son Shining.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the Bian garrison mutinied, killing adjutant Cao Jin'an and magistrate Li Mai and plotting to install Xuanzuo's son Shining.

sentences.zh: 上將遣兵送湊赴鎮，召宰臣議。

translations.literal: The emperor was about to send troops to escort Cou to his post and summoned the chief ministers to discuss.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was about to send troops to escort Cou to his command and summoned the chief ministers to discuss the matter.

sentences.zh: 竇參深沮其行，恐軍中拒命，乃召湊回，授右金吾衛大將軍，而以梁宋節鉞授士寧。

translations.literal: Dou Can strongly obstructed the journey, fearing the army would refuse orders; he recalled Cou and made him right general of the Golden Guard, while giving the Liang-Song commission to Shining.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Can blocked the move, fearing the troops would refuse to obey; he recalled Cou, made him right general of the Golden Guard, and gave the Liang-Song commission to Shining instead.

sentences.zh: 春夏旱，穀貴，人多流亡。

translations.literal: Drought in spring and summer; grain was dear; many people fled as refugees.
translations.idiomatic: Spring and summer brought drought; grain prices soared, and many people fled their homes.

sentences.zh: 京兆尹韓臯以政事不理黜官。

translations.literal: Metropolitan Governor Han Gao was dismissed for poor administration.
translations.idiomatic: Metropolitan Governor Han Gao was dismissed for mismanaging affairs.

sentences.zh: 上召湊，面授京兆尹，即日令視事，經宿方下制。

translations.literal: The emperor summoned Cou, personally appointed him metropolitan governor of Jingzhao, that same day ordered him to assume duties; the formal edict came only after one night.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned Cou, personally appointed him metropolitan governor of Jingzhao, and had him take office that same day; the formal edict followed only after a night had passed.

sentences.zh: 湊孜孜為理，以勤儉為務，人樂其政。

translations.literal: Cou worked diligently at governance, made thrift his task; the people rejoiced in his administration.
translations.idiomatic: Cou governed with tireless diligence and made thrift his watchword; the people welcomed his rule.

sentences.zh: 時宮中選內官買物於市，倚勢強買物，不充價，人畏而避之，呼為「宮市」。

translations.literal: At the time the palace selected eunuchs to buy goods in the market; relying on power they forcibly bought goods without paying full price; people feared and avoided them, calling it the "Palace Market."
translations.idiomatic: At the time the palace sent eunuchs into the markets to buy goods; trading on their power, they seized merchandise without paying fair price. People feared them and stayed away, calling the practice the Palace Market.

sentences.zh: 掌賦者多與中貴人交結假借，不言其弊。

translations.literal: Those in charge of tax levies mostly associated with palace favorites and lent their power, not speaking of the abuses.
translations.idiomatic: Most tax officials cultivated ties with palace favorites and lent them their authority, saying nothing about the abuses.

sentences.zh: 湊為京尹，便殿從容論之，曰：「物議以中人買物於市，稍不便於人，此事甚細，虛掇流議。

translations.literal: As metropolitan governor, in the informal hall Cou spoke at ease on it, saying: "Public talk holds that palace agents buying in the market is somewhat inconvenient for people; the matter is very minor, yet stirs idle rumor.
translations.idiomatic: As metropolitan governor, Cou raised the matter at ease in the informal hall: "Public talk holds that palace agents buying in the market is a nuisance to the people. The affair is trifling, yet it stirs idle rumor.

sentences.zh: 凡宮中所須，責臣可辦，不必更差中使。

translations.literal: Whatever the palace requires, your subject can supply; there is no need to send palace envoys again.
translations.idiomatic: Whatever the palace needs, your subject can provide it; there is no need to dispatch palace envoys again.

sentences.zh: 若以臣府縣外吏，不合預聞宮中所須，則乞選內官年高謹重者，充宮市令，庶息人間論議。」

translations.literal: If as a prefecture-county official outside the palace I ought not hear of palace needs, then I beg to select aged, grave eunuchs to serve as Palace Market commissioners, so as to quiet public talk."
translations.idiomatic: If a prefectural official like me ought not even hear of palace needs, then I beg that aged, prudent eunuchs be chosen as Palace Market commissioners, so public talk may quiet down."

sentences.zh: 又奏：「掌閑彍騎、飛龍內園、芙蓉及禁軍諸司等使，雜供手力資課太多，量宜減省。」

translations.literal: He also memorialized: "The commissioners of palace leisure, guard cavalry, Flying Dragon inner gardens, Hibiscus, and various palace guard offices levy too much corvée labor and supplies; they should appropriately be reduced."
translations.idiomatic: He also memorialized: "The commissioners of palace leisure, guard cavalry, Flying Dragon inner gardens, Hibiscus, and the various palace guard offices levy far too much corvée labor and supplies; these levies should be cut back as appropriate."

sentences.zh: 上多從之。

translations.literal: The emperor largely agreed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor largely agreed.

sentences.zh: 初，府掾吏以湊起自戚籓，不諳簿領，凡有疑獄難決之事，多候湊將出時方呈，冀免指擿瑕病。

translations.literal: At first, clerks of the prefecture, because Cou had risen from a consort kin post and was unfamiliar with ledgers, when there were doubtful cases hard to decide mostly waited until Cou was about to leave before presenting them, hoping to avoid having flaws pointed out.
translations.idiomatic: At first the prefectural clerks, thinking Cou had risen from consort kin circles and knew little of ledgers, waited until he was about to leave before presenting doubtful cases they could not resolve, hoping to escape having their faults exposed.

sentences.zh: 湊雖倉卒閱視，必指其奸幸之處，下筆決斷，無毫厘之差。

translations.literal: Cou, though reviewing in haste, always pointed out the fraudulent favored spots, decided with his brush, without the slightest error.
translations.idiomatic: Even when he reviewed cases in haste, Cou always found the points of fraud and favoritism and decided them with his brush without the slightest error.

sentences.zh: 掾吏非大過，不行笞責；

translations.literal: For clerks without great faults, he did not apply beating punishment;
translations.idiomatic: For clerks whose faults were not grave, he did not have them beaten;

sentences.zh: 而召面按問，詰責而釋之。

translations.literal: but summoned them face to face for inquiry, reprimanded and released them.
translations.idiomatic: he summoned them for questioning face to face, rebuked them, and let them go.

sentences.zh: 吏尤惕厲，庶務咸舉。

translations.literal: The clerks became especially vigilant; all routine affairs were properly handled.
translations.idiomatic: The clerks grew all the more wary, and every routine matter was properly handled.

sentences.zh: 文敬太子、義章公主相繼薨歿，上深追念，葬送之儀頗厚。

translations.literal: Crown Prince Wenjing and Princess Yizhang died in succession; the emperor deeply mourned them; funeral rites were quite lavish.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Wenjing and Princess Yizhang died in succession. The emperor mourned them deeply, and their funeral rites were lavish.

sentences.zh: 召集工役，載土築墳，妨民農務。

translations.literal: He summoned laborers to haul earth and build tombs, obstructing the people's farm work.
translations.idiomatic: Laborers were summoned to haul earth and raise tombs, disrupting the people's farm work.

sentences.zh: 湊候上顧問，極言之。

translations.literal: Cou waited for when the emperor asked his opinion and spoke to the utmost.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor asked his view, Cou spoke out as forcefully as he could.

sentences.zh: 宗屬門吏以湊論諫太繁，恐上厭苦，每以簡約規之。

translations.literal: Household clerks of the imperial clan, because Cou's remonstrances were too frequent, feared the emperor would grow weary; they often advised him to be brief.
translations.idiomatic: Clerks in the imperial clan household, fearing the emperor would weary of Cou's many remonstrances, often urged him to be brief.

sentences.zh: 湊曰：「聖上明哲，憂勞四海，必不以公主、太子之鐘念而忽疲民。

translations.literal: Cou said: "The sage ruler is enlightened, laboring over all under heaven; he will surely not, for lingering grief over the princess and crown prince, neglect the weary people.
translations.idiomatic: Cou said: "Our sage ruler is enlightened and toils for all under heaven. He will surely not, for lingering grief over the princess and crown prince, neglect a people already worn down.

sentences.zh: 但人多順旨不言，若再三啟諫，必動宸情，則生民受賜。

translations.literal: But many people follow the imperial will and do not speak; if one remonstrates again and again, it will surely move the imperial heart, and then the living people will receive the benefit.
translations.idiomatic: But most people simply follow the imperial will and keep silent. If one remonstrates again and again, the emperor's heart will surely be moved, and the people will benefit.

sentences.zh: 長吏不言，是為阿旨。

translations.literal: For a chief official not to speak is to flatter the imperial will.
translations.idiomatic: For a chief official to keep silent is to flatter the throne.

sentences.zh: 如窮民上訴，罪在何人？」

translations.literal: If the poor people appeal above, on whom will the guilt fall?"
translations.idiomatic: If the poor appeal above, on whom will the blame fall?"

sentences.zh: 議者重之。

translations.literal: Commentators held him in esteem.
translations.idiomatic: Commentators respected him for it.

sentences.zh: 以能政，兼兵部尚書。

translations.literal: For capable administration, he was additionally made minister of war.
translations.idiomatic: For his able governance he was additionally made minister of war.

sentences.zh: 官街樹缺，所司植榆以補之，湊曰：「榆非九衢之玩。」

translations.literal: Official avenues lacked trees; the responsible office planted elms to fill the gaps; Cou said: "Elms are not fitting for the nine thoroughfares."
translations.idiomatic: Where official avenues lacked trees, the responsible office planted elms to fill the gaps. Cou said: "Elms are not fit for the capital's great thoroughfares."

sentences.zh: 亟命易之以槐。

translations.literal: He immediately ordered them replaced with locust trees.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately ordered them replaced with locust trees.

sentences.zh: 及槐陰成而湊卒，人指樹而懷之。

translations.literal: When the locust shade had grown and Cou died, people pointed to the trees and remembered him.
translations.idiomatic: When the locust shade had grown and Cou died, people pointed to the trees and remembered him fondly.

sentences.zh: 湊於德宗為老舅，漢魏故事，多退居散地，才免罪戾而已。

translations.literal: Cou was Dezong's maternal uncle by marriage; in Han and Wei precedent, such men mostly retired to sinecure posts, barely escaping guilt and punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Cou was Dezong's maternal uncle by marriage. Han and Wei precedent mostly kept such men in idle posts, barely spared from disgrace.

sentences.zh: 湊自貞元已來，特承恩顧，歷中外顯貴，雖聖獎隆深，亦由湊小心辦事，奉職有方故也。

translations.literal: Since Zhenyuan Cou had enjoyed special favor, serving in prominent posts at court and abroad; though the sage's praise was deep, it was also because Cou was careful in handling affairs and served his duties with method.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Zhenyuan era Cou had enjoyed special favor and held prominent posts at court and in the provinces. Though the emperor's praise ran deep, it owed much to Cou's careful handling of affairs and steady service.

sentences.zh: 湊既疾，不召巫醫，藥不入口，家人泣而勉之。

translations.literal: When Cou fell ill, he did not summon shamans or physicians; medicine did not enter his mouth; his family wept and urged him.
translations.idiomatic: When Cou fell ill he would not call shamans or physicians and would take no medicine. His family wept and pleaded with him.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「吾以凡才，濫因外戚進用，起家便授三品，歷顯位四十年，壽登七十，為人足矣，更欲何求？

translations.literal: He replied: "I am a man of ordinary talent, unworthily advanced through consort kin ties; at the start of my career I was given third rank, held prominent posts for forty years, reached seventy years of life — enough for a man; what more do I seek?
translations.idiomatic: He replied: "I am a man of ordinary talent, unworthily raised through consort kin ties. At the start of my career I was given third rank, held high office for forty years, and have reached seventy — enough for any man. What more could I want?

sentences.zh: 古之以親戚進用者，罕有善終，吾得歸全以侍先人，幸也。」

translations.literal: Of old those advanced through kin ties rarely had good endings; that I may die whole and join my ancestors is fortune."
translations.idiomatic: Of old, consort kin raised to power rarely died in peace. That I may end whole and join my ancestors is fortune enough."

sentences.zh: 德宗知之，令御醫進藥，不獲已，服之。

translations.literal: When Dezong learned, he ordered the imperial physician to bring medicine; unable to refuse, Cou took it.
translations.idiomatic: When Dezong learned of this, he sent the imperial physician with medicine. Unable to refuse, Cou took it.

sentences.zh: 四月卒，時年七十一，贈尚書左僕射，罷朝一日。

translations.literal: He died in the fourth month, aged seventy-one; posthumously made left vice director of the Department of State Affairs; court suspended for one day.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fourth month at seventy-one. He was posthumously made left vice director of the Department of State Affairs, and court business was suspended for one day.

sentences.zh: 竇覦

translations.literal: Dou Yu
translations.idiomatic: Dou Yu

sentences.zh: 竇覦，昭成皇后族侄。

translations.literal: Dou Yi was a clansman nephew of Empress Zhaocheng.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Yi was a clansman nephew of Empress Zhaocheng.

sentences.zh: 父光，華原尉。

translations.literal: His father Guang was ward commander of Huayuan.
translations.idiomatic: His father Guang served as ward commander of Huayuan.

sentences.zh: 覦以親廕，釋褐右衛率府兵曹參軍。

translations.literal: Yi entered office through kin privilege as army adjutant of the Right Guard colonel's office.
translations.idiomatic: Yi entered office through kin privilege as army adjutant in the Right Guard colonel's office.

sentences.zh: 鄜坊節度臧希讓奏為判官，累授監察殿中侍御史、檢校工部員外郎、坊州刺史，

translations.literal: Zang Xirang, military governor of Fufang, recommended him as aide; he was successively made supervising censor, palace censor, acting vice minister of works, and prefect of Fang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zang Xirang, military governor of Fufang, recommended him as aide. He rose through supervising censor, palace censor, acting vice minister of works, and prefect of Fang.

sentences.zh: 討李懷光於河中，詔覦以坊州兵七百人屯邰陽。

translations.literal: Campaigning against Li Huaiguang at Hezhong, an edict ordered Yi to station seven hundred Fang Prefecture troops at Taiyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Huaiguang was attacked at Hezhong, an edict ordered Yi to station seven hundred Fang troops at Taiyang.

sentences.zh: 賊平，以功兼御史中丞。

translations.literal: When the rebels were pacified, for merit he was additionally made censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebels were crushed, he was additionally made censor-in-chief for his service.

sentences.zh: 遷同州刺史，入朝為戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to prefect of Tong Prefecture, entered court as vice minister of revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to prefect of Tong, then entered court as vice minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 覦無他才伎，為吏有計數，又以韓滉子婿，故籓府辟召，遂歷牧守。

translations.literal: Yi had no other talent or skill; as an official he was calculating; also as Han Huang's son-in-law, he was recruited by provincial governments and thus served as prefect and governor.
translations.idiomatic: Yi had no other gifts. As an official he was shrewd, and as Han Huang's son-in-law he was repeatedly recruited by provincial governments, eventually serving as prefect and governor.

sentences.zh: 宰相竇參，覦再從侄。

translations.literal: Chancellor Dou Can was Yi's second cousin once removed.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Dou Can was Yi's second cousin once removed.

sentences.zh: 參少依覦，及參秉政，力薦於朝，故有貳卿之拜。

translations.literal: Can in youth relied on Yi; when Can held power, he strongly recommended him at court; hence the appointment as second-ranked minister.
translations.idiomatic: Can had relied on Yi in youth; once in power he pushed hard for him at court, which earned Yi a second-ranked ministerial appointment.

sentences.zh: 數月，為揚州大都督府長史、御史大夫、充淮南節度副大使、知節度事，既非德舉，人咸薄之。

translations.literal: Within months he was made chief administrator of Yangzhou grand protectorate, censor-in-chief, deputy military governor of Huainan and acting governor; since it was not a merit appointment, all looked down on him.
translations.idiomatic: Within months he was made chief administrator of Yangzhou, censor-in-chief, deputy military governor of Huainan, and acting governor. Since the appointment owed nothing to merit, everyone looked down on him.

sentences.zh: 赴鎮旬日，暴卒，詔贈禮部尚書。

translations.literal: Ten days after reaching his post he died suddenly; an edict posthumously made him minister of rites.
translations.idiomatic: Ten days after reaching his post he died suddenly. An edict posthumously made him minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 柳晟

translations.literal: = Liu Sheng =
translations.idiomatic: = Liu Sheng =

sentences.zh: 柳晟者，肅宗皇后之甥。

translations.literal: Liu Sheng was a nephew of Emperor Suzong's empress.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Sheng was a nephew of Emperor Suzong's empress.

sentences.zh: 母和政公主。

translations.literal: His mother was Princess Hezheng.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was Princess Hezheng.

sentences.zh: 父潭，官至太僕卿、駙馬都尉。

translations.literal: His father Tan rose to minister of imperial stud and commandant-escort.
translations.idiomatic: His father Tan rose to minister of the imperial stud and commandant-escort.

sentences.zh: 晟少無檢操，代宗於諸甥之中，特加撫鞠，俾與太子、諸王同學，授詩書，恩寵罕比。

translations.literal: Sheng in youth lacked restraint; among all his nephews Daizong especially nurtured him, had him study with the crown prince and princes, taught him the classics; favor rarely matched.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng was unrestrained in youth. Among all his nephews Daizong singled him out for nurture, had him study with the crown prince and the princes, and taught him the classics. Few enjoyed such favor.

sentences.zh: 累試太常卿。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly tried as minister of imperial observances.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly appointed minister of imperial observances on probation.

sentences.zh: 德宗即位，以與晟幼同硯席，尤親之。

translations.literal: When Dezong ascended, because he had shared desk and mat with Sheng in youth, he was especially close to him.
translations.idiomatic: When Dezong ascended the throne, he was especially close to Sheng because they had shared desk and mat as boys.

sentences.zh: 涇師之亂，從幸奉天，晟密啟曰：「願受詔入京城，遊說群賊，冀其攜貳。」

translations.literal: During the Jingzhou mutiny, following the emperor to Fengtian, Sheng secretly reported: "I wish to receive an edict to enter the capital and win over the rebel bands, hoping they will split and waver."
translations.idiomatic: During the Jingzhou mutiny, as the emperor fled to Fengtian, Sheng secretly reported: "I beg to receive an edict to enter the capital and win over the rebel bands, hoping to divide their loyalties."

sentences.zh: 德宗壯而許之。

translations.literal: Dezong admired this and agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong admired his courage and agreed.

sentences.zh: 晟與賊帥多有舊，出入其門說誘之。

translations.literal: Sheng had old ties with many rebel leaders; he entered and left their gates to persuade them.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng had old ties with many rebel leaders and went in and out among them to win them over.

sentences.zh: 事泄，為硃泚所擒，械之於獄。

translations.literal: The plot leaked; Zhu Ci captured him and shackled him in prison.
translations.idiomatic: The plot leaked. Zhu Ci captured him and shackled him in prison.

sentences.zh: 晟有力，乃於獄中穿垣破械而遁，落發為僧，間道歸行在。

translations.literal: Sheng was strong; he broke through the prison wall and shattered his shackles to escape, shaved his head as a monk, and by hidden paths returned to the imperial camp.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng was strong. He broke through the prison wall, shattered his shackles, shaved his head as a monk, and by hidden paths made his way back to the imperial camp.

sentences.zh: 遷將作少監。

translations.literal: He was promoted to vice director of palace construction.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice director of palace construction.

sentences.zh: 元和初，檢校工部尚書、興元尹、山南西道節度使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanhe, acting minister of works, governor of Xingyuan, military governor of Shannan West Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Yuanhe he was made acting minister of works, governor of Xingyuan, and military governor of Shannan West Circuit.

sentences.zh: 罷鎮入朝，以違詔進奉，為御史元稹所劾，詔宥之。

translations.literal: After leaving his post he entered court; for submitting tribute in violation of an edict he was impeached by censor Yuan Zhen; an edict pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: After leaving his post he returned to court. Censor Yuan Zhen impeached him for submitting tribute in violation of an edict, but an imperial pardon spared him.

sentences.zh: 俄充入回鶻冊立使，復命，遷左金吾衛大將軍。

translations.literal: Soon he served as envoy to invest the Uyghur khan; on return he was made left general of the Golden Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he served as envoy to invest the Uyghur khan. On his return he was made left general of the Golden Guard.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈太子少保。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously made junior tutor to the heir.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made junior tutor to the heir.

sentences.zh: 王子顏

translations.literal: Wang Ziyan
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ziyan

sentences.zh: 王子顏，瑯邪臨沂人，莊憲皇后之父也。

translations.literal: Wang Ziyan, a man of Langya Linyi, was the father of Empress Zhuangxian.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ziyan, a native of Langya Linyi, was the father of Empress Zhuangxian.

sentences.zh: 祖思敬，少從軍，累試太子賓客。

translations.literal: His grandfather Sijing entered the army in youth; repeatedly tried as grand mentor of the heir.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Sijing entered the army in youth and was repeatedly appointed grand mentor of the heir on probation.

sentences.zh: 父難得，有勇決，善騎射，天寶初為河源軍使。

translations.literal: His father Nan De was bold and resolute, skilled at mounted archery; at the beginning of Tianbao he was commissioner of Heyuan Army.
translations.idiomatic: His father Nan De was bold and resolute and skilled at mounted archery. At the beginning of the Tianbao era he served as commissioner of the Heyuan Army.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃贊普王子郎支都有勇，乘諳真馬，寶鈿裝鞍，出陣求鬥，無敢與校者。

translations.literal: The Tibetan emperor's son Langzhidu was brave; riding a well-trained horse with jeweled saddle trappings, he came out to challenge; none dared contend with him.
translations.idiomatic: The Tibetan emperor's son Langzhidu was a fierce warrior. Riding a well-trained horse with a jeweled saddle, he rode out to challenge the Tang lines, and none dared meet him.

sentences.zh: 難得挾槍奮馬突前，刺殺郎支都，斬其首，傳於京師。

translations.literal: Nan De grasped his lance, spurred his horse forward, stabbed and killed Langzhidu, cut off his head, and sent it to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Nan De seized his lance, spurred his horse forward, ran Langzhidu through, cut off his head, and sent it to the capital.

sentences.zh: 軍還，玄宗召見之，令於殿前乘馬挾槍作刺郎支都之狀。

translations.literal: When the army returned, Xuanzong summoned him and had him ride before the hall with lance in hand, reenacting the killing of Langzhidu.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned, Xuanzong summoned him and had him ride before the hall with lance in hand, reenacting the killing of Langzhidu.

sentences.zh: 賜以錦袍金帶，累拜金吾將軍同正員，

translations.literal: He was granted brocade robe and gold belt; successively made regular captain of the Golden Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted a brocade robe and gold belt and was successively promoted to regular captain of the Golden Guard.

sentences.zh: 從哥舒翰擊吐蕃於積石，虜吐谷渾王子悉弄參及子婿悉頰藏而還，累拜左武衛將軍、關西遊奕使。

translations.literal: Following Geshu Han he struck the Tibetans at Jishi, captured Tuyuhun prince Sinong Can and his son-in-law Sinu Cang and returned; successively made general of the Left Martial Guard and roaming inspector of Guanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Following Geshu Han he struck the Tibetans at Jishi, captured the Tuyuhun prince Sinong Can and his son-in-law Sinu Cang, and returned. He was successively made general of the Left Martial Guard and roaming inspector of Guanxi.

sentences.zh: 九載，擊吐蕃，收五橋，拔樹敦城，補白水軍使。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he struck Tibet, took Wuqiao, captured Shudun city, and was made commissioner of Baishui Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he attacked Tibet, took Wuqiao, captured Shudun city, and was made commissioner of the Baishui Army.

sentences.zh: 十三載，從收九曲，加特進。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he followed in recovering the Nine Bends and was granted extraordinary promotion.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he took part in recovering the Nine Bends and was granted extraordinary promotion.

sentences.zh: 祿山之叛，從哥舒翰戰於潼關；

translations.literal: When An Lushan rebelled, he fought with Geshu Han at Tong Pass;
translations.idiomatic: When An Lushan rebelled, he fought with Geshu Han at Tong Pass;

sentences.zh: 關門不守，從肅宗幸靈武。

translations.literal: when the pass fell, he followed Suzong to Lingwu.
translations.idiomatic: when the pass fell, he followed Suzong to Lingwu.

sentences.zh: 時行在闕軍賞，難得進絹三千疋及金銀器等。

translations.literal: At the time the mobile court lacked funds for military rewards; Nan De presented three thousand bolts of silk and gold and silver vessels.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the mobile court lacked funds for military rewards. Nan De presented three thousand bolts of silk and gold and silver vessels.

sentences.zh: 至德初，試衛尉卿、興平軍使，兼鳳翔都知兵馬使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhide he was tried as minister of the guard, commissioner of Xingping Army, and concurrently director of military affairs at Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Zhide era he was appointed minister of the guard, commissioner of the Xingping Army, and concurrently director of military affairs at Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 進收京城，與賊軍戰。

translations.literal: Advancing to recover the capital, he fought the rebel army.
translations.idiomatic: Advancing to recover the capital, he fought the rebel army.

sentences.zh: 其下靳元曜戰酣墮馬，難得馳救之，賊射之中眉，皮穿披下鄣目。

translations.literal: His subordinate Jin Yuanyao, fighting fiercely, fell from his horse; Nan De galloped to rescue him; rebels shot him in the brow; the skin tore and the cheek flap of his helmet hung down over his eyes.
translations.idiomatic: His subordinate Jin Yuanyao, fighting fiercely, was thrown from his horse. Nan De galloped to his rescue, but rebels shot him in the brow; the skin tore and the cheek flap of his helmet fell over his eyes.

sentences.zh: 難得自拔去箭，並皮掣洛，馳馬復戰，血流被面，而抗賊不已。

translations.literal: Nan De pulled out the arrow himself, tearing skin as he yanked it free, spurred his horse back into battle; blood covered his face, yet he fought the rebels without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Nan De pulled out the arrow himself, skin tearing as he yanked it free, then spurred his horse back into battle. Blood covered his face, yet he kept fighting the rebels without pause.

sentences.zh: 肅宗深嘉之。

translations.literal: Suzong deeply praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Suzong praised him deeply.

sentences.zh: 從郭子儀攻安慶緒於相州，累封瑯邪郡公，英武軍使。

translations.literal: Following Guo Ziyi he attacked An Qingxu at Xiang Prefecture; successively enfeoffed Duke of Langya Commandery and commissioner of the Yingwu Army.
translations.idiomatic: Following Guo Ziyi he attacked An Qingxu at Xiang. He was successively enfeoffed Duke of Langya and made commissioner of the Yingwu Army.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈潞州大都督。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously made grand governor of Lu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made grand governor of Lu.

sentences.zh: 子顏少從父征役，累官金紫光祿大夫、檢校衛尉卿，生后而卒。

translations.literal: Ziyan in youth followed his father on campaigns; rose to grand master of golden light and acting minister of the guard; he died after the empress was born.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyan followed his father on campaign from youth and rose to grand master of golden light and acting minister of the guard. He died after the empress was born.

sentences.zh: 順宗內禪，以后生憲宗皇帝，褒贈先代：思敬司徒，難得太傅，子顏太師。

translations.literal: When Shunzong abdicated inwardly and the empress bore Emperor Xianzong, previous generations were honored posthumously: Sijing as grand tutor, Nan De as grand preceptor, Ziyan as grand master.
translations.idiomatic: When Shunzong abdicated and the empress bore Emperor Xianzong, earlier generations were honored posthumously: Sijing as grand tutor, Nan De as grand preceptor, and Ziyan as grand master.

sentences.zh: 顏子重榮，官至福王傅；

translations.literal: Ziyan's son Chongrong rose to tutor of the Prince of Fu;
translations.idiomatic: Ziyan's son Chongrong rose to tutor of the Prince of Fu;

sentences.zh: 用，官至太子賓客、金吾將軍。

translations.literal: Yong rose to grand mentor of the heir and general of the Golden Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Yong rose to grand mentor of the heir and general of the Golden Guard.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：戚里之賢，避寵畏權。

translations.literal: Praise says: Among worthy consort kin, some shunned favor and feared power.
translations.idiomatic: In praise: Among worthy consort kin, some shunned favor and feared power.

sentences.zh: 不恤禍患，鮮能保全。

translations.literal: Those who did not heed calamity rarely preserved themselves whole.
translations.idiomatic: Those who ignored the threat of ruin rarely kept themselves whole.

sentences.zh: 福盈者敗，勢壓者顛。

translations.literal: Those who overflow with good fortune are ruined; those whose momentum presses down are overturned.
translations.idiomatic: When blessing overflows, ruin follows; when power presses too hard, it topples.

sentences.zh: 武之惟良，明於自然。

translations.literal: Of the Wu clan, Weiliang alone understood what is natural.
translations.idiomatic: Among the Wu, only Weiliang grasped the way things naturally are.
